# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kerberos (RFC 4120), TCP and UDP port 88 -- the first Windows AD-suite protocol (see
# kerberos.hpp's file header comment for the wire format, structural detection gate, and the
# curated attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_kerberos_sample -- tests/sample_kerberos.pcap (UDP, 15 packets) and
# tests/sample_kerberos_tcp.pcap (TCP, 3 packets: one whole frame, one split across two segments).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME kerberos_as_req_no_preauth_standing_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_req_no_preauth_standing_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REQ cname=alice sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM realm=\"EXAMPLE\\.COM\" etype=\\[aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96,aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96,rc4-hmac\\]\n *note: AS-REQ has no PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP pre-authentication data -- AS-REP-Roasting-style request shape")

# The FLAGSHIP AS-REP-Roasting note: only fires on the successful AS-REP that correlates (by
# cname, on the same session) to an earlier no-preauth AS-REQ -- see kerberos.cpp's
# KerberosFlowState::pending_as_req.
add_test(NAME kerberos_as_rep_roasting_flagship_note_correlated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_rep_roasting_flagship_note_correlated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=rc4-hmac\n *note: AS-REP Roasting: this is a successful, crackable AS-REP answering an AS-REQ \\(packet #1\\) that included no pre-authentication proof -- the target account likely has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled")

add_test(NAME kerberos_tgs_req_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_tgs_req_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REQ cname=\\(none\\) sname=cifs/fileserver\\.example\\.com realm=\"EXAMPLE\\.COM\"")

# The FLAGSHIP Kerberoasting note: keys off the embedded Ticket's OWN enc-part etype (RC4 here),
# not the response's own outer enc-part etype (deliberately left AES in this fixture to prove the
# two are checked independently -- see kerberos.cpp's Note 2 comment).
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_flagship_note_correlated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_flagship_note_correlated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=cifs/fileserver\\.example\\.com enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96\n *note: this service ticket's encrypted part uses rc4-hmac -- crackable offline if this SPN's account is compromised via Kerberoasting")

# Kerberoasting must NOT fire on a krbtgt sname (an ordinary TGT, not a service ticket) even with
# an RC4 ticket enc-part -- see kerberos.cpp's own exclusion comment.
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_excludes_krbtgt_sname
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_excludes_krbtgt_sname PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM[^\n]*\n *note: this service ticket")

# Kerberoasting negative control: a real (non-krbtgt) SPN whose ticket enc-part is AES (a fully
# patched, AES-only domain) must not be flagged either.
add_test(NAME kerberos_kerberoasting_negative_control_aes_ticket
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_kerberoasting_negative_control_aes_ticket PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  TGS-REP cname=alice ticket-sname=ldap/dc1\\.example\\.com enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ticket-sname=ldap/dc1\\.example\\.com[^\n]*\n *note: this service ticket")

# The negative case for the roasting FLAGSHIP note itself: ordinary Windows-style behavior --
# no-preauth AS-REQ, KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED, a RETRY that DOES include PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP, then a
# successful AS-REP -- must NOT get the flagship note. Proves correlation tracks the most recent
# request for a given cname (the retry overwrites the pending entry), not just the first attempt.
add_test(NAME kerberos_as_rep_roasting_negative_case_normal_retry_not_flagged
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_kerberos.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(kerberos_as_rep_roasting_negative_case_normal_retry_not_flagged PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[kerberos\\]  AS-REP cname=bob ticket-sname=krbtgt/EXAMPLE\\.COM enc-part-etype=aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "cname=bob[^\n]*\n *note: AS-REP Roasting")

add_test(NAME kerberos_krb_error_named_codes_decoded

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LDAP (RFC 4511), TCP/389 and TCP/3268 (Global Catalog) -- the second Windows AD-suite protocol
# (see ldap.hpp's file header comment for the wire format -- IMPLICIT tagging, NOT Kerberos's own
# EXPLICIT convention -- the structural detection gate/collision survey, and the six curated
# attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_ldap_sample()
# -- tests/sample_ldap.pcap (TCP, 62 packets across 17 independent sessions/flows A-Q) and
# tests/sample_ldap_tcp_split.pcap (TCP, 2 packets: one SearchRequest split across two segments).
# All expectations below were captured from the actual built binary's output against these
# fixtures (the same "manual smoke test BEFORE writing CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline the
# Kerberos delivery's own verification step used), not hand-computed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Curated note 3 (SPN sweep) plus the example filter rendering ldap.hpp's own header comment

# The "keep state across many SearchResultEntry responses, close on the terminal
# SearchResultDone" correlation shape -- genuinely new relative to Kerberos's own strict 1:1
# pairing (see ldap.hpp's own STATE/CORRELATION section).

# SearchResultEntry attribute-value rendering, including the "(N bytes, binary)" fallback for a

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "BindRequest id=1 version=3 dn=\"cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com\" auth=simple credential=12 byte\\(s\\), not decoded[^\n]*\n *note: credential sent in cleartext \\(simple bind with a non-empty password\\) with no prior StartTLS")

# Curated note 2 NEGATIVE control -- the SAME cleartext simple bind shape, but preceded by a
# StartTLS ExtendedRequest/ExtendedResponse on the SAME session: must NOT fire.
add_test(NAME ldap_bind_cleartext_suppressed_after_starttls_negative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ldap.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ldap_bind_cleartext_suppressed_after_starttls_negative PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "ExtendedRequest id=1 name=StartTLS \\(1\\.3\\.6\\.1\\.4\\.1\\.1466\\.20037\\).*ExtendedResponse id=1 resultCode=success name=1\\.3\\.6\\.1\\.4\\.1\\.1466\\.20037.*BindRequest id=2 version=3 dn=\"cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com\" auth=simple credential=12 byte\\(s\\), not decoded"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "BindRequest id=2 version=3 dn=\"cn=admin[^\n]*\n *note: credential sent in cleartext")

# Curated note 2 NEGATIVE control -- a SASL GSSAPI bind (a negotiated, non-cleartext mechanism
# other than PLAIN) with no StartTLS: must NOT fire, even though a credential is present.
add_test(NAME ldap_bind_sasl_gssapi_not_flagged_negative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ldap.pcap" --format text)

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "auth=SASL\\(GSSAPI\\)[^\n]*\n *note: credential sent in cleartext")

# Curated note 2 positive via the SASL path -- SASL PLAIN carries an authzid\\0authcid\\0password

# Curated note 4 -- AS-REP-Roasting target discovery via the AD bitwise-AND matching rule against

# Note 4/5 NEGATIVE control -- the SAME bitwise-AND mechanism against an unrelated bit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SMB2/NTLM (MS-SMB2/MS-NLMP), TCP/445 and TCP/139 -- the third Windows AD-suite protocol (see
# smb.hpp's/ntlm.hpp's own file header comments for the wire format -- fixed-width little-endian
# fields, NOT BER like Kerberos/LDAP -- the structural detection gate, compounding, and the six
# curated attack/monitoring notes). Fixtures generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_smb_sample() -- tests/sample_smb.pcap (TCP, 26 packets across 7 independent
# sessions/flows A-G) and tests/sample_smb_tcp_split.pcap (TCP, 2 packets: one NEGOTIATE Request
# split across two segments). All expectations below were captured from the actual built binary's
# output against these fixtures -- confirmed first via an independent, hand-built synthetic
# exchange (the same "manual smoke test BEFORE writing CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline
# Kerberos's/LDAP's own deliveries used), not hand-computed or guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# NEGOTIATE Request's dialect list (including the 0x02FF multi-protocol wildcard) and Response's
# negotiated dialect, plus curated note 2 POSITIVE -- SecurityMode SIGNING_ENABLED but NOT
# SIGNING_REQUIRED, the ntlmrelayx precondition.
add_test(NAME smb_negotiate_dialects_and_note2_positive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_negotiate_dialects_and_note2_positive PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 2\\.0\\.2, SMB 2\\.1, SMB 3\\.0, SMB 3\\.0\\.2, SMB 3\\.1\\.1, SMB 2\\.\\?\\?\\? \\(multi-protocol negotiate wildcard\\)\\).*SMB2 NEGOTIATE Response \\(SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\) \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: SMB signing is enabled but NOT required on this session -- the precondition every NTLM-relay tool \\(ntlmrelayx and equivalents\\) checks for")

# Curated note 2 NEGATIVE control -- SecurityMode SIGNING_ENABLED|SIGNING_REQUIRED on the SAME
# NEGOTIATE Response shape (flow D): must NOT fire.
add_test(NAME smb_negotiate_signing_required_note2_negative_control
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_negotiate_signing_required_note2_negative_control PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "52504 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\)  \\(client"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\) -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52504  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Response \\(SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\) \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: SMB signing")

# Full NTLM negotiate/challenge/authenticate handshake -- curated note 3 fires on EVERY
# NTLM-bearing message (not just once), and the terminal SESSION_SETUP Response closes the
# SessionId-keyed multi-leg handshake with a "succeeded" correlation note (the genuinely new
# correlation shape relative to Kerberos's/LDAP's own 1:1/keep-until-terminal pairings).
add_test(NAME smb_ntlm_handshake_note3_and_succeeded_correlation
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_ntlm_handshake_note3_and_succeeded_correlation PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SMB2 SESSION_SETUP Request \\(NEGOTIATE_MESSAGE\\)[^\n]*\n *note: NTLM authentication in use for this session \\(NEGOTIATE_MESSAGE\\).*SMB2 SESSION_SETUP Response \\(CHALLENGE_MESSAGE\\) \\[STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED\\][^\n]*\n *note: NTLM authentication in use for this session \\(CHALLENGE_MESSAGE\\).*SMB2 SESSION_SETUP Request \\(AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE\\)[^\n]*\n *note: NTLM authentication in use for this session \\(AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE\\).*SMB2 SESSION_SETUP Response \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: NTLM handshake for CORP, succeeded")

# Curated note 5, both forms -- a TREE_CONNECT path ending in "$" is flagged preliminarily on the

# Security rule (smb.hpp's/ntlm.hpp's own file header comment): LmChallengeResponse/
# NtChallengeResponse/EncryptedRandomSessionKey are NEVER rendered, in any form -- not the raw
# bytes, not even presence/length -- anywhere in this decoder's JSON output, only
# ntlm_user_name/ntlm_domain_name (identity, not proof-of-possession material). Checked against
# the AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE emitted for flow A's own successful handshake.
add_test(NAME smb_json_ntlm_credential_material_never_rendered
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(smb_json_ntlm_credential_material_never_rendered PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"ntlm_message_type\": \"AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE\",\n *\"ntlm_user_name\": \"jdoe\",\n *\"ntlm_domain_name\": \"CORP\","
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "lm_challenge|nt_challenge|LmChallenge|NtChallenge|session_key|\\\\xAA\\\\xAA|\\\\xBB\\\\xBB")

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[modbus\\]")

# SMB is GateKind::TcpPortIndependent -- a NEGOTIATE exchange on an arbitrary, non-configured TCP
# port (4455, not 445/139) must still be recognized as smb, with a "not a configured/standard SMB
# port" note on BOTH directions of the session.
add_test(NAME smb_nonstandard_port_recognized_with_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_nonstandard_port_recognized_with_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52507 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4455  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\)[^\n]*\n *note: seen on TCP port 52507->4455, which is not a configured/standard SMB port \\(445/139\\).*192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4455 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52507  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Response \\(SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\) \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: SMB signing is enabled but NOT required[^\n]*\n *note: seen on TCP port 4455->52507, which is not a configured/standard SMB port \\(445/139\\)")

# --smb-port suppresses just the non-standard-port note, not detection itself.
add_test(NAME smb_port_option_suppresses_nonstandard_port_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb.pcap" --smb-port 4455 --format text)
set_tests_properties(smb_port_option_suppresses_nonstandard_port_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:52507 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:4455  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard SMB port")

# Exercises smb_tcp_declared_length via Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload -- unlike LDAP's own split
# test, SMB2 DOES have its own 4-byte length prefix (like Kerberos's).
add_test(NAME smb_tcp_segment_split_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_smb_tcp_split.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(smb_tcp_segment_split_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[tcp\\]  buffering a SMB message \\(MS-SMB2\\) PDU/frame split across TCP segments 51420->445: 57 of 114 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more.*\\[smb\\]  SMB2 NEGOTIATE Request \\(dialects: SMB 2\\.0\\.2, SMB 2\\.1, SMB 3\\.0, SMB 3\\.0\\.2, SMB 3\\.1\\.1\\)[^\n]*\n *note: reassembled a SMB message \\(MS-SMB2\\) PDU/frame from 114 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments on this flow")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Netlogon/DCE-RPC (MS-NRPC/MS-RPCE), carried inside SMB2 WRITE/READ/IOCTL against a tracked
# "\PIPE\netlogon" FileId -- the fourth and final Windows AD-suite protocol (see dcerpc.hpp's/
# netlogon.hpp's own file header comments for the wire format -- the generic DCE/RPC PDU
# envelope, NDR conformant-varying strings, the FileId->bind->call_id correlation depth, and
# the five curated notes). No independent wire gate: this traffic is recognized only via a
# tracked FileId opened against a pipe share whose CREATE Name (after stripping a leading
# \PIPE\ prefix) equals "netlogon". Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_netlogon_sample() -- tests/sample_netlogon.pcap (TCP, 142 packets across 9 independent
# flows A-I): A) a normal ReqChallenge->NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake for WIN10-PC$ (note 1
# positive, notes 2/3/4 negative controls); B) an all-zero-ClientChallenge NetrServerReqChallenge
# from "ATTACKER-PC" (note 2 positive -- the Zerologon wire signature); C) a
# NetrServerAuthenticate2 handshake for LEGACY-PC$ (note 3 positive, note 1 positive); D) a
# NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake with AccountName "WORKSTATION1" not ending in "$" despite a
# WorkstationSecureChannel type (note 4 positive, note 1 positive); E) the same shape with
# AccountName "WORKSTATION1$" (note 4 negative control, note 1 positive); F) a
# NetrServerPasswordSet2 call for WIN10-PC$ (note 5 positive); G) a NetrServerPasswordSet2 call
# sent sealed (RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY) -- exercises the "sealed, N bytes, not decoded"
# fallback, no notes; H) a bind to a non-Netlogon interface UUID on a netlogon-named pipe --
# exercises the bind-interface-confirmation gate, structural-only, no notes; a bare
# NetrLogonUasLogon-shaped CREATE against pipe name "lsarpc" -- proves an untracked pipe name
# never even reaches the DCE/RPC parser (zero dcerpc_messages emitted); I) the same handshake as
# flow A for WIN10-PC$ but carried over IOCTL/FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE instead of WRITE+READ (note 1
# positive, proving both real-world transport shapes decode identically). All expectations below
# were captured from the actual built binary's output against this fixture -- confirmed via
# direct --format text/--format json/--stats inspection (the "manual smoke test BEFORE writing
# CMakeLists.txt tests" discipline every prior phase's delivery used), not hand-computed or
# guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# CREATE request decodes the pipe Name (stripped of any \PIPE\ prefix); CREATE response decodes
# the 16-byte FileId -- both fields smb.hpp/smb.cpp read for the very first time this phase,
# needed regardless of Netlogon since neither was read at all before.
add_test(NAME netlogon_create_request_and_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_create_request_and_response_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"create_name\": \"netlogon\",.*\"file_id\": \"0000000000000002:00000000f00d0002\",")

# NetrServerReqChallenge (opnum 4) request/response field decode -- PrimaryName (unique
# pointer)/ComputerName (ref pointer)/ClientChallenge (presence via client_credential_all_zero
# only, never the raw 8 bytes).
add_test(NAME netlogon_reqchallenge_request_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_reqchallenge_request_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"primary_name\": \"DC1\",\n *\"computer_name\": \"WIN10-PC\",\n *\"client_credential_all_zero\": false,\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge computer=WIN10-PC\"")

add_test(NAME netlogon_reqchallenge_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_reqchallenge_response_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": true,\n *\"status_name\": \"STATUS_SUCCESS\",\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge response status=STATUS_SUCCESS\"")

# NetrServerAuthenticate3 (opnum 26) request/response field decode -- AccountName/
# SecureChannelType (the 16-bit NDR enum, named)/NegotiateFlags/AccountRid, the fullest-decoded
# opnum this phase has.
add_test(NAME netlogon_authenticate3_request_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_authenticate3_request_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3\",\n *\"call_id\": 4,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"primary_name\": \"DC1\",\n *\"account_name\": \"WIN10-PC\\$\",\n *\"computer_name\": \"WIN10-PC\",\n *\"secure_channel_type\": \"WorkstationSecureChannel\",\n *\"client_credential_all_zero\": false,\n *\"negotiate_flags\": 1630535679,\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3 account=WIN10-PC\\$\"")

add_test(NAME netlogon_authenticate3_response_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_authenticate3_response_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3\",\n *\"call_id\": 4,\n *\"is_response\": true,\n *\"account_rid\": 1105,\n *\"status_name\": \"STATUS_SUCCESS\",\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerAuthenticate3 response status=STATUS_SUCCESS\"")

# Curated note 1 -- closing correlation on the terminal NetrServerAuthenticate3 response for flow
# A's tracked pipe conversation (WRITE+READ transport).
add_test(NAME netlogon_secure_channel_established_note1_positive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SMB2 READ Response \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: Netlogon secure channel established for WIN10-PC\\$ \\(NetrServerAuthenticate3, status=STATUS_SUCCESS\\)")

# Curated note 2 POSITIVE -- an all-zero NetrServerReqChallenge ClientChallenge, the Zerologon
# (CVE-2020-1472) wire signature -- both the text note and the JSON field
# (client_credential_all_zero: true, never the raw bytes).
add_test(NAME netlogon_zerologon_zero_challenge_note2_positive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_zerologon_zero_challenge_note2_positive PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SMB2 WRITE Request  \\(client 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -- port-heuristic\\)\n *note: Netlogon ClientChallenge is all-zero bytes -- the wire signature of CVE-2020-1472 \\(\"Zerologon\"\\); a real challenge is an 8-byte random nonce, so this essentially never occurs in benign traffic, though presence alone does not prove a completed compromise")

add_test(NAME netlogon_zerologon_zero_challenge_json_field
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_zerologon_zero_challenge_json_field PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"computer_name\": \"ATTACKER-PC\",\n *\"client_credential_all_zero\": true,\n *\"summary\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge computer=ATTACKER-PC challenge=ALL-ZERO\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "client_credential_hex|client_challenge_hex")

# Curated note 2 NEGATIVE control -- flow A's own NetrServerReqChallenge (frame #9, a genuine
# random-looking 8-byte challenge) must NOT fire the all-zero note.

# Curated note 3 POSITIVE -- legacy NetrServerAuthenticate2 (opnum 15) used instead of the modern
# NetrServerAuthenticate3 (opnum 26), plus its own JSON field decode (flow C, LEGACY-PC$).
add_test(NAME netlogon_legacy_authenticate2_note3_positive

add_test(NAME netlogon_legacy_authenticate2_json_fields

# Curated note 4 POSITIVE -- AccountName "WORKSTATION1" claims a WorkstationSecureChannel type
# but does not end in "$" (flow D).

# Curated note 5 -- NetrServerPasswordSet2 observed (flow F), the literal post-Zerologon
# password-reset step; deliberately NOT sticky (fires every occurrence, unlike notes 2-4). JSON
# check doubles as the "password material never rendered" test: only authenticator_present (bool)
# and clear_new_password_length (int) are emitted, never the Authenticator/ClearNewPassword bytes
# themselves -- the same posture NTLM's own LmChallengeResponse/NtChallengeResponse test enforces.
add_test(NAME netlogon_password_set2_note5_and_material_never_rendered

add_test(NAME netlogon_password_set2_json_fields_material_never_rendered

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "clear_new_password\"|authenticator\"|clear_new_password_hex|authenticator_hex")

add_test(NAME netlogon_password_set2_response_json_fields

# Sealed-call fallback (flow G, RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY): auth_level and sealed=true are
# read from the sec_trailer's own unencrypted fixed header, but the stub is never parsed as
# plaintext NDR -- an honest "sealed, N bytes, not decoded" summary with no account/credential
# fields at all, and (see the negative-control test below) no curated note fires from it either.
add_test(NAME netlogon_sealed_call_fallback_json

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": 30,\n *\"auth_level\": \"RPC_C_AUTHN_LEVEL_PKT_PRIVACY\",\n *\"sealed\": true,\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC request \\(opnum 30\\)\"[^\n]*\n *\\}\n *\\],\n *\"netlogon_calls\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"opnum\": \"NetrServerPasswordSet2\",\n *\"call_id\": 16,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"sealed\": true,\n *\"summary\": \"sealed, 32 bytes, not decoded\"")

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "sealed")

# Bind-interface-confirmation gate (flow H): a bind to a non-Netlogon abstract syntax UUID on a
# netlogon-named pipe leaves the context's later request/response pairs structural-only (opnum
# numeric, no netlogon_calls emitted at all) -- the defensive edge case where the pipe NAME alone
# is not trusted as proof of which RPC interface is actually bound.
add_test(NAME netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_structural_only_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bind_contexts\": \\[\\{\"context_id\": 0, \"abstract_syntax_uuid\": \"367abb81-9844-35f1-ad32-98f038001003\", \"is_netlogon\": false\\}\\],\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC bind\".*\"opnum\": 4,\n *\"summary\": \"DCE/RPC request \\(opnum 4\\)\"\n *\\}\n *\\],\n *\"summary\": \"SMB2 WRITE Request\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"NetrServerReqChallenge\",\n *\"call_id\": 18")

add_test(NAME netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_no_curated_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_no_curated_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n#111  [0-9.]+  192\\.168\\.1\\.50:53007 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:445 \\(microsoft-ds\\)  \\[smb\\]  SMB2 WRITE Request  \\(client 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -- port-heuristic\\)\n#112  ")

# Flow H's own pipe is named "lsarpc" -- since the SAMR/LSARPC batch (this file's own later
# lsarpc_* tests), that name IS now tracked, so this is no longer a never-parsed negative control
# (an earlier revision of this test predates LSARPC support and asserted the opposite). What it
# actually exercises now: flow H's own bind negotiates the NETLOGON interface UUID on this
# "lsarpc"-named pipe (a deliberately mismatched pipe-name/interface-UUID combination), so the
# envelope IS parsed (dcerpc_messages appears, is_netlogon: true on the bind) but LsarpcPipeState's
# own bound_context_is_interface check (is_lsarpc_interface_uuid) never accepts it -- the LSARPC-side
# analog of netlogon_non_netlogon_interface_bind_structural_only_json above, proven by no
# "lsarpc_calls"/"samr_calls" key ever appearing for this FileId.
add_test(NAME lsarpc_pipe_name_netlogon_interface_bind_never_lsarpc_calls_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(lsarpc_pipe_name_netlogon_interface_bind_never_lsarpc_calls_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"create_name\": \"lsarpc\",.*\"file_id\": \"000000000000000a:00000000f00d000a\",\n *\"dcerpc_messages\": \\[\n *\\{\n *\"ptype\": \"bind\",.*\"abstract_syntax_uuid\": \"12345678-1234-abcd-ef00-01234567cffb\", \"is_netlogon\": true"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"(lsarpc|samr)_calls\"")

# Both real-world transport shapes decode identically -- flow I repeats flow A's own
# ReqChallenge->NetrServerAuthenticate3 handshake for WIN10-PC$, but carried over
# IOCTL/FSCTL_PIPE_TRANSCEIVE instead of WRITE+READ.
add_test(NAME netlogon_ioctl_pipe_transceive_transport_note1_positive
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(netlogon_ioctl_pipe_transceive_transport_note1_positive PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "SMB2 IOCTL Response \\[STATUS_SUCCESS\\][^\n]*\n *note: Netlogon secure channel established for WIN10-PC\\$ \\(NetrServerAuthenticate3, status=STATUS_SUCCESS\\)")

# --stats netlogon opnum counts -- NetrServerAuthenticate2=1 (flow C), NetrServerAuthenticate3=4
# (flows A/D/E/I), NetrServerPasswordSet2=2 (flow F unsealed + flow G sealed -- counted from the
# cleartext opnum in the DCE/RPC request header regardless of sealing), NetrServerReqChallenge=3
# (flows A/B/I).
add_test(NAME netlogon_stats_opnum_counts
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_netlogon.pcap" --stats)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DRSUAPI (MS-DRSR), phase 3 of the SAMR/LSARPC/SRVSVC/WKSSVC/DRSUAPI batch -- see drsuapi.hpp's
# own file header comment for the wire format, the narrow four-opnum coverage table, and --
# critically -- the EMPIRICALLY-DISCOVERED SCOPE CAVEAT: real DRSUAPI traffic predominantly rides
# a dynamically-negotiated raw TCP connection (resolved via the port-135 endpoint mapper), not an
# SMB named pipe, so this decoder (and the fixture below) only ever demonstrate the narrow "also
# exposed over a named pipe" case, not real-world DCSync traffic as it actually appears on the
# wire. Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_drsuapi_sample() --
# tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap (TCP, 3 independent flows A-C -- see that function's own doc comment
# for the full per-flow breakdown). All expectations below were captured from the actual built
# binary's output against this fixture -- confirmed via direct --format text/--format json/--stats
# inspection, not hand-computed or guessed at.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME drsuapi_create_request_pipe_name_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(drsuapi_create_request_pipe_name_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"create_name\": \"drsuapi\",")

# DRSBind (0) request/response -- non-NULL puuidClientDsa (full field decode), and a response whose
# own DRS_EXTENSIONS payload is a deliberately non-4-byte-aligned 3 bytes -- proving
# skip_drs_extensions' own trailing-pad computation doesn't misalign the phDrs/status fields that
# follow it (both are correctly decoded here, not garbage/misaligned).
add_test(NAME drsuapi_bind_request_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(drsuapi_bind_request_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"DRSBind\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"client_dsa_guid\": \"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee\",\n *\"summary\": \"DRSBind client_dsa=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee\"")

add_test(NAME drsuapi_bind_response_json_fields_skip_extensions
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(drsuapi_bind_response_json_fields_skip_extensions PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"DRSBind\",\n *\"call_id\": 3,\n *\"is_response\": true,\n *\"handle\": \"0101010101010101010101010101010101010101\",\n *\"status_name\": \"ERROR_SUCCESS\",\n *\"summary\": \"DRSBind response status=ERROR_SUCCESS\""
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "999999")

# DRSBind (0) request again -- NULL puuidClientDsa this time: negative control, no client_dsa_guid
# field at all (the regex below requires is_response/summary to be textually ADJACENT to call_id 4,
# so any intervening client_dsa_guid line would break the match).
add_test(NAME drsuapi_bind_null_client_dsa_negative_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_drsuapi.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(drsuapi_bind_null_client_dsa_negative_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"DRSBind\",\n *\"call_id\": 4,\n *\"is_response\": false,\n *\"summary\": \"DRSBind\"\n *\\}")

# DRSUnbind (1) request/response -- handle decode both directions (request carries the SAME handle
# DRSBind's own response returned; response carries the zeroed handle MS-DRSR's own convention
# returns on success).
add_test(NAME drsuapi_unbind_request_json_fields

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"opnum\": \"DRSBind\",\n *\"call_id\": 12")

# --stats drsuapi opnum counts -- DRSGetNCChanges counts 3 (two unsealed occurrences in flow A plus

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# QUIC -- Tier 2, joining HTTPS (see quic.hpp's own file header comment and notable_it_protocols.hpp
# for why). tests/sample_quic.pcap (tools/make_quic_sample_pcap.py) has 13 packets: #1 a genuine
# client Initial, decrypted end to end with its ClientHello SNI extracted; #2 Version Negotiation;
# #3-5 Handshake/0-RTT/Retry, each name-only but each now requiring the per-type structural
# cross-check described below; #6 a short-header (1-RTT) packet, the weakest, port-only fallback;
# #7 an Initial whose AEAD tag doesn't verify (simulating a server's own Initial, which this decoder
# can never decrypt -- see quic.hpp's file header comment); #8 non-QUIC junk on QUIC's own default
# port, proving no false positive; #9 a short-header packet on a non-standard port, proving that
# fallback's own internal port gate; #10 (round-one bug fix regression, see below) a 0-RTT-shaped
# packet whose byte0 satisfies Header Form/Fixed Bit/type bits but whose trailer is NOT structurally
# self-consistent, proving it now falls through to generic "udp" rather than being misdetected;
# #11-12 (round-two bug fix regression, see below) an Initial-shaped packet whose Token-Length/
# Length-field pair both decode to 0, and a Retry-shaped packet whose Version isn't QUIC v1 --
# proving both now fall through to generic "udp" too; #13 (round-two positive control) a genuinely
# truncated real v1 Initial packet (a plausible, large Length field, but far fewer bytes actually
# captured), proving round two's fix didn't also reject legitimate truncated captures. See
# decoder.cpp's own dispatch-ordering comment (just above its HART-IP UDP check) for why QUIC's
# recognition call had to move ahead of HART-IP's: QUIC v1's Version field lands on the exact same
# two payload bytes HART-IP's own MessageType/MessageID gate reads, and is SYSTEMATICALLY 0x00/0x00
# there for every long-header packet type this fixture exercises -- a guaranteed collision, not a
# coincidental one.
#
# Bug fix, round one (post-release, Jurgen's own report): packets #3-5's own Handshake/0-RTT/Retry
# recognition originally accepted ANY long-header packet whose byte0 had the Header Form bit, Fixed
# Bit, and a non-Initial type value set -- only 4 bits of the whole packet, true of roughly 1 in 4
# arbitrary UDP payloads port-independently. A real capture proved this too weak: a busy NBT-NS
# (UDP port 137) broadcast segment's own 2-byte Transaction ID landed on byte0/byte1 often enough to
# misdetect a large fraction of that segment's non-NBT-NS-parsing traffic as QUIC 0-RTT/Handshake
# packets. Fixed by requiring the same kind of self-consistent structural cross-check every other
# long-header type already had (Version Negotiation's own whole-number-of-4-byte-versions check;
# Initial's own Length-field/captured-bytes cross-check): 0-RTT/Handshake now read their own Length
# field (RFC 9000 17.2.3/17.2.4) and require it to describe a byte count that actually fits within
# what was captured and is at least large enough for a 1-byte Packet Number plus a 16-byte AEAD tag;
# Retry now requires its own mandatory 16-byte Retry Integrity Tag (RFC 9000 17.2.5) to actually be
# present. See try_recognize_quic's own comment in quic.cpp for the full writeup, and packet #10
# above/quic_0rtt_type_bits_alone_not_misdetected below for the regression test.
#
# Bug fix, round two (post-release, Jurgen's own SECOND report, against the same real NBT-NS
# capture): round one's own checks were each individually still too weak. Retry's "16 trailing bytes
# exist" check is true of nearly any ordinary-sized UDP payload (Retry has no Length field to
# cross-check at all -- see quic.cpp's own comment for why not), so it now also requires an exact
# QUIC-v1 Version match. Initial's pre-existing Length-field check conflated two different failure
# modes into one tolerant "truncated capture" fallback: `length_field < 17` (structurally impossible
# for a real Initial packet, any capture length) was treated the same as `pn_offset + length_field >
# captured size` (a plausible field that just wasn't fully captured -- genuine truncation); only the
# second one still gets the tolerant match now. See try_recognize_quic's own comment in quic.cpp for
# the full writeup, and packets #11-13 above / the three quic_*_round_two_* tests below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME quic_client_initial_decrypted_sni
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_quic.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(quic_client_initial_decrypted_sni PROPERTIES

add_test(NAME stats_mode_rip

# Too little follows the fixed header to attempt an embedded-datagram parse at all (see
# decode_embedded_datagram's own >=20-byte gate) -- summary must stop right after the code name,
# no "-- original datagram" fragment, and the JSON must omit icmp_embedded_datagram entirely
# (conditional emission, same convention as every other optional field in output.cpp).

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_icmp.pcap" --format json)

# Regression test for a real collision found while adding this decoder: FF-HSE's own opportunistic,
# any-port structural gate is weak enough that it was accepting a synthetic HSRPv1 message on port
# 1985 as truncated FF-HSE traffic before RIP/HSRP were moved ahead of FF-HSE in decoder.cpp's UDP
# dispatch chain (see the comment there). This must decode as hsrp, never ffhse.
add_test(NAME hsrp_not_misdetected_as_ffhse
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hsrp.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(hsrp_not_misdetected_as_ffhse PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  .*\\[hsrp\\]  HSRPv1 Hello")

add_test(NAME hsrp_invalid_payload_not_misdetected

set_tests_properties(hsrp_invalid_payload_not_misdetected PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 5 byte\\(s\\) on port 1985->1985")

# Finding 2, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch160.md: a malicious if_tsresol
# byte could declare a units-per-second figure that doesn't fit in a uint64_t, making
# fill_pcapng_timestamp's static_cast<uint64_t>(...) undefined behavior (pcap_reader.cpp). Fixed
# by bounding the exponent before computing it (parse_if_tsresol_option) plus a defense-in-depth
# clamp at the conversion site itself (fill_pcapng_timestamp). sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng
# (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_pcapng_implausible_tsresol_sample) has three interfaces:
# 0 (binary, exponent 127 -- far past the 63 boundary), 1 (decimal, exponent 100 -- far past the
# 19 boundary), both of which must fall back to the same microsecond default this function
# already uses for a malformed option; and 2 (binary, exponent 63 -- exactly the largest power of
# two that still fits in a uint64_t), which must NOT fall back, proving the boundary itself isn't
# off-by-one rejected. The whole point of this test is simply that decoding completes cleanly and
# produces this exact, deterministic output instead of crashing or invoking UB -- a golden-output
# test, the same bar every other exact-value test in this file is held to, confirmed against the
# actual CLI before being written here (not guessed at). Packet 3's own oddly large negative
# relative timestamp is a legitimate, defined consequence of interface 2's own genuinely absurd
# (2^63 units/second) but in-bounds resolution -- not a defect this fix introduces or needs to
# smooth over; only interfaces 0 and 1 (the ones actually being tested for the fallback) need to
# look sane, and they do (a clean 1-microsecond delta between packets 1 and 2, exactly what
# falling back to the 1e6 default on both produces).
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_falls_back_without_ub
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_falls_back_without_ub PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0.000000[^\n]*\n.*\n#2  0.000001[^\n]*\n.*\n.*\n#3  -1699999999.999816")

add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_completes_all_three_packets
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_completes_all_three_packets PROPERTIES
  # Each packet's own index+timestamp pair (adjacent lines, confirmed against the real JSON
  # output first) -- proves all three packets decoded cleanly: interfaces 0/1's implausible
  # exponents both falling back to the same 1e6 default (hence identical whole-second epoch,
  # 1-microsecond apart), interface 2's boundary case computing its own (legitimately odd, see
  # the text-format test above) but still well-defined result. Three independent checks in one
  # regex (rather than one long chain spanning all three packet objects) to avoid depending on
  # every field in between, which is unrelated to what this test is actually confirming.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 1,\n *\"timestamp\": 1700000000.000000,")
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet2_timestamp
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet2_timestamp PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 2,\n *\"timestamp\": 1700000000.000001,")
add_test(NAME pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet3_timestamp
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_pcapng_implausible_tsresol.pcapng" --format json)
set_tests_properties(pcapng_implausible_tsresol_json_packet3_timestamp PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"index\": 3,\n *\"timestamp\": 0.000184,")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# terminal_escape (output.cpp, finding 4, docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-patch160.md):
# packet-derived text (here, an MQTT PUBLISH topic straight off the wire) can carry raw C0 control
# bytes, including ESC (0x1B). TextWriter/FieldsWriter used to write such text straight to the
# real terminal -- an attacker-controlled capture could therefore emit real ANSI escape sequences
# (manipulating the analyst's terminal, e.g. faking colored alert text) or raw newlines (forging
# fake extra packet lines). terminal_escape() renders every C0/DEL byte as a literal "\xNN" escape
# instead, in TEXT-mode output only -- JSON/CSV keep their own existing, different, complete
# escaping rules untouched (json_escape already renders ESC as \u001b; CSV is deliberately left
# as-is per the review's own guidance). The fixture's two packets carry a raw ESC-based ANSI
# injection attempt and a raw-newline forgery attempt respectively; both are confirmed against the
# actual CLI output below, not guessed at.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_ansi_injection_sanitized_in_text_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_ansi_injection_sanitized_in_text_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x1b\\[31mFAKE-ALERT\\\\x1b\\[0m\" qos=0")

add_test(NAME terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_text_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_text_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x0afake-injected-line\" qos=0")

# FieldsWriter (-T fields) has its own, separate route to the terminal: it round-trips each field
# through a one-shot JSON encode/decode (json_escape then json_unescape_inner) to build the flat
# text representation. json_unescape_inner deliberately restores \n/\t/\r to raw bytes (but leaves
# \uXXXX, including ESC's \u001b, as literal text) -- so FieldsWriter was already safe against the
# ESC-specific attack above, but not against a restored raw newline forging an extra output line.
# This confirms terminal_escape() closes that second, independent gap too.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_fields_output
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" -T fields -e summary)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_newline_injection_sanitized_in_fields_output PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "PUBLISH topic=\"evil\\\\x0afake-injected-line\" qos=0")

# JSON output must be unaffected by terminal_escape (it is never applied to JsonWriter): the raw
# ESC byte still comes through json_escape's own existing \u001b control-character escaping,
# exactly as before this fix.
add_test(NAME terminal_escape_json_output_unaffected_still_uses_u001b
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_terminal_escape_injection.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(terminal_escape_json_output_unaffected_still_uses_u001b PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"PUBLISH topic=\\\\\"evil\\\\u001b\\[31mFAKE-ALERT\\\\u001b\\[0m\\\\\" qos=0")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolver (resolver.hpp/resolver.cpp): OUI (MAC vendor) resolution (off by default, --mac-vendor, to
# keep output compact), hostname resolution (off by default, --resolve/--hosts, file-only --
# never live DNS), and service name resolution (on by default, --nn/--services) -- see
# decoder.cpp's src_mac/dst_mac gap-fix and output.cpp's TextWriter/JsonWriter/CsvWriter for how
# these are rendered. All tests below use tests/sample_modbus.pcap, whose two endpoints' MACs
# (00:0c:29:11:22:33/00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc) are both in oui_table.gen.hpp's MA-L table as "VMware",
# and tests/hosts_sample.txt / tests/services_sample.txt (see their own file headers) as the
# --hosts/--services fixtures.
#
# In TEXT output specifically, the entire "eth <src> -> <dst>" line is itself gated behind
# --ether (off by default, mirrors tcpdump's own -e -- see output.hpp/output.cpp's show_mac_;
# --ether has no short alias of its own in this codebase -- -e is reserved for -T fields' own
# --field, tshark's own convention -- see the "-T fields / -e / -f / -c / -a / -w / -x" section
# further down).
# --mac-vendor implies --ether (cli_main.cpp: there'd be nothing to attach a vendor name to
# otherwise), so --mac-vendor alone still shows the full "eth <mac> (<vendor>) -> <mac> (<vendor>)"
# line. --ether alone shows the MAC pair with no vendor annotation. JSON/CSV are NOT gated by
# --ether at all -- src_mac/dst_mac stay unconditional base fields there (like src_ip/dst_ip)
# regardless of --ether; --mac-vendor only ever controls their *_mac_vendor annotation fields, in
# every format.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

set(RESOLVER_HOSTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/hosts_sample.txt")
set(RESOLVER_SERVICES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/services_sample.txt")

# --- --ether (the eth line itself), off by default, text-output only ---------------------

add_test(NAME resolver_mac_and_vendor_hidden_by_default_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_mac_and_vendor_hidden_by_default_text PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|VMware")

add_test(NAME resolver_ether_flag_shows_mac_without_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_ether_flag_shows_mac_without_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "VMware")

# --- OUI (MAC vendor) vendor annotation, off by default, --mac-vendor opts in (and implies --ether) -----

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_vendor_hidden_by_default_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_vendor_hidden_by_default_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_mac\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\","
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "_mac_vendor")

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(VMware\\) -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(VMware\\)")

# --mac-vendor alone (no explicit --ether) must still show the eth line -- --mac-vendor implies --ether (cli_main.cpp).
add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_alone_implies_ether_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_alone_implies_ether_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33")

add_test(NAME resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --mac-vendor --format json)
set_tests_properties(resolver_oui_flag_shows_vendor_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"src_mac\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\",\n *\"dst_mac\": \"00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\",\n *\"src_mac_vendor\": \"VMware\",\n *\"dst_mac_vendor\": \"VMware\",")

# src_mac/dst_mac themselves (the base gap-fix, independent of OUI resolution and of --ether)
# are always present for an Ethernet-linktype capture in JSON/CSV, even with OUI resolution left
# at its off-by-default posture -- this is the actual base value, not an annotation, so OUI
# resolution only ever adds a vendor name, never gates the MAC itself. --ether only affects
# TEXT output (see this section's own header comment above) -- CSV keeps showing it regardless.
add_test(NAME resolver_base_src_dst_mac_always_present_in_csv_regardless_of_oui_or_ether
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format csv)
set_tests_properties(resolver_base_src_dst_mac_always_present_in_csv_regardless_of_oui_or_ether PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33,00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc,,,")

# tests/sample_modbus.pcap's own two addresses are the only ones hosts_sample.txt names; no other
# IP appears in this capture, so a positive "hostname resolution finds nothing when nothing
# matches" case is instead covered directly against Resolver's own file-parsing rules by the two
# duplicate-IP/first-wins fixture lines in hosts_sample.txt (see its own file header) -- exercised
# implicitly by the assertion above ("plc-01", not "should-never-win", for 192.168.1.10).
add_test(NAME resolver_hosts_file_first_occurrence_wins_not_last
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --resolve --hosts "${RESOLVER_HOSTS}" --format text)
set_tests_properties(resolver_hosts_file_first_occurrence_wins_not_last PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "should-never-win")

# Gap fix (a necessary, deliberate part of this feature, not scope creep -- see resolver.hpp's
# file header and docs/MANUAL.md): src_mac/dst_mac are now rendered for EVERY protocol on an
# Ethernet-linktype capture, not just the raw-Ethernet ones (GOOSE/SV/EtherCAT/PROFINET/STP) whose
# own MAC-bearing fields (stp_root_mac/etc.) were already shown. sample_enip.pcap is a plain
# IPv4-based protocol (EtherNet/IP explicit messaging over TCP) that never had any MAC output at
# all before this feature.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enip.pcap" --ether --format text)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[enip\\].*\n *eth 00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VLAN ID display (output.cpp's TextWriter/JsonWriter/CsvWriter show_vlan_; --no-vlan in
# cli_main.cpp). DecodedPacket::has_vlan_tag/vlan_id are already unconditionally populated by the
# decoding layer for every Ethernet-linktype packet (link_layer.cpp's parse_ethernet unwraps a
# single 802.1Q tag) -- this is purely a display toggle, shown by default. tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap
# (see build_vlan_zones_sample in tools/make_sample_pcap.py) carries VLAN 100, VLAN 200, and one
# untagged flow, so it exercises both "tagged" and "untagged" in the same capture.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# VLAN display is independent of --ether (show_mac_) -- see output.hpp/output.cpp's own
# comments -- so a VLAN-tagged packet still gets its own "vlan <id>" line by default. Every packet
# in this fixture is non-IP (PROFINET RT/GOOSE/SV/EtherCAT), so its src_mac/dst_mac already appear
# directly on the headline itself (output.cpp's endpoint() -- see that function's own comment) with
# no --ether/--mac-vendor needed at all; there is deliberately no separate "eth <mac> -> <mac>" prefix line for
# a non-IP packet any more (write_packet() suppresses it there specifically, since it would just
# repeat what the headline already shows), so this fixture no longer has one to test.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\][^\n]*\n *vlan 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\n *eth ")

# --ether is now a no-op for this fixture (every packet is non-IP, so show_mac_'s own separate line
# never applies here regardless -- see this section's own header comment) -- kept as an explicit
# regression check that --ether doesn't reintroduce a combined "eth ... vlan ..." line for a non-IP
# packet the way it did before this behavior changed.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_stays_on_own_line_with_ether_for_non_ip_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --ether --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_stays_on_own_line_with_ether_for_non_ip_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\][^\n]*\n *vlan 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29")

# The untagged flow (mac pair 00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88) must never get a "vlan ..."
# suffix at all -- has_vlan_tag is false, not vlan_id == 0. No --ether needed any more: the untagged
# packet's own MAC pair is already on its headline by default (see this section's own header
# comment), same as every other packet in this fixture.
add_test(NAME vlan_id_omitted_for_untagged_packet_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_omitted_for_untagged_packet_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88[^\n]*\\[ethercat\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88[^\n]*\n *vlan")

# The MAC pair fallback itself needs neither --ether nor --mac-vendor -- it's unconditional for any
# non-IP packet (see endpoint()'s own comment) -- but the vendor-name annotation next to it still
# needs --mac-vendor explicitly (Resolver::oui_vendor() self-gates on that flag). Confirms neither flag is
# now accidentally implied by MAC display working out of the box.
add_test(NAME non_ip_mac_shown_by_default_without_vendor_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(non_ip_mac_shown_by_default_without_vendor_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:cc:55:66 -> 00:0c:29:dd:77:88"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|VMware")

add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"dst_mac\": \"00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\",\n *\"has_vlan_tag\": true,\n *\"vlan_id\": 100,")

# The untagged flow gets has_vlan_tag: false / vlan_id: null, never omitted entirely -- unlike an
# annotation, has_vlan_tag/vlan_id are always both present together when the flag is on, regardless
# of whether this particular packet actually carries a tag (mirrors policy_engine.cpp's own
# EthernetFlowReport JSON convention).
add_test(NAME vlan_id_null_for_untagged_packet_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_null_for_untagged_packet_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"has_vlan_tag\": false,\n *\"vlan_id\": null,")

add_test(NAME vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format csv)
set_tests_properties(vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "profinet,\"Cyclic RT IO data \\(RT_CLASS_1, unicast\\): 8 byte\\(s\\) IO data, cycle_counter=4660 data_status=\\[Primary,Valid,Run,Ok\\] transfer_status=OK\",,100")

# --no-vlan suppresses the "  vlan 100" suffix; the headline's own MAC pair (unconditional for a
# non-IP packet, see this section's own header comment) is unaffected either way. --ether is included
# here purely as a regression check that it still doesn't reintroduce anything.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan --ether)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc[^\n]*\\[profinet\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "vlan 100|eth 00:0c:29")

# Same, without --ether: the whole vlan line disappears, the MAC pair stays exactly as it was.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_and_no_ether_suppresses_entire_eth_line_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_and_no_ether_suppresses_entire_eth_line_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|vlan 100")

add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_json
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format json --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_json PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "has_vlan_tag|vlan_id")

add_test(NAME no_vlan_suppresses_display_csv
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format csv --no-vlan)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_suppresses_display_csv PROPERTIES
  # vlan_id (empty, suppressed by --no-vlan) is immediately followed by the trailing `time` column
  # (see time_format.hpp/output.cpp's `-t`/--time-format/--time-offset) -- relative's default
  # rendering is elapsed-since-first-packet, so this pcap's first packet is asserted literally as
  # 0.000000 here, same "hardcode this sample's known value" style vlan_id_shown_by_default_csv
  # above already uses for its own trailing column. `time` is no longer the row's last column --
  # direction_source/direction_client_ip (empty here: this is a raw PROFINET RT frame, not TCP, so
  # FlowDirectionTracker never touches it -- see CsvWriter::write_packet) now follow it, hence the
  # two trailing empty fields before the newline.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "profinet,\"Cyclic RT IO data \\(RT_CLASS_1, unicast\\): 8 byte\\(s\\) IO data, cycle_counter=4660 data_status=\\[Primary,Valid,Run,Ok\\] transfer_status=OK\",,,0\\.000000,,\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "transfer_status=OK\",,100")

# --mac-vendor and --no-vlan are independent toggles -- suppressing VLAN display must not affect the
# vendor annotation either way. --mac-vendor alone (no --ether) is enough here: the vendor name attaches
# directly to the headline's own MAC pair for a non-IP packet like this one, no separate eth line
# involved any more -- see this section's own header comment.
add_test(NAME no_vlan_does_not_affect_oui
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_vlan_zones.pcap" --format text --no-vlan --mac-vendor)
set_tests_properties(no_vlan_does_not_affect_oui PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(VMware\\) -> 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(VMware\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "eth 00:0c:29|vlan 100")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `-t`/`--time-format` mnemonics (time_format.hpp/time_format.cpp; TextWriter's leading "#<index>
# <time>" header -- see output.cpp's own use of TimeRenderer). sample_modbus.pcap's own 3 packets
# (see tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_modbus_sample) have known, fixed timestamps: 1700000000
# .000000, 1700000001.001000, 1700000002.002000 -- exactly 1.001s / 1.001s apart -- deliberately
# uneven spacing so relative/delta/epoch are all distinguishable from each other in the assertions
# below, not just from zero. This section previously had no dedicated coverage at all (only one
# CSV test elsewhere incidentally hardcoded the epoch-format value of a different pcap's first
# packet) -- added here as part of flipping the default from epoch to relative, so the default
# this project now actually ships is verified, not just the explicit mnemonics.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# r/relative, the default: elapsed since the first packet, so packet 1 is always 0.000000
# regardless of its raw epoch value.
add_test(NAME time_format_relative_is_the_default
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(time_format_relative_is_the_default PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1\\.001000  .*\n.*#3  2\\.002000  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_r_mnemonic_same_as_relative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t r)
set_tests_properties(time_format_r_mnemonic_same_as_relative PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  ")

# e/epoch: raw seconds since the Unix epoch, unchanged from the pcap's own timestamp field.
add_test(NAME time_format_epoch_explicit_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t epoch)
set_tests_properties(time_format_epoch_explicit_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  1700000000\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1700000001\\.001000  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_e_mnemonic_same_as_epoch
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t e)
set_tests_properties(time_format_e_mnemonic_same_as_epoch PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  1700000000\\.000000  ")

# The raw "timestamp" JSON field is always the epoch double, regardless of -t -- only the "time"
# field it sits alongside is affected. Asserted here with the default (relative) -t left in place,
# to prove -t's default change doesn't leak into the machine-parseable raw field.
add_test(NAME time_format_does_not_affect_raw_timestamp_json_field
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(time_format_does_not_affect_raw_timestamp_json_field PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"timestamp\": 1700000000\\.000000,.*\"time\": \"0\\.000000\"")

# d/delta: elapsed since the previous packet -- packet 1 has no previous packet, so it's 0.000000
# same as relative; packets 2 and 3 are both 1.001000 apart despite different relative offsets,
# which is exactly what distinguishes delta from relative.
add_test(NAME time_format_delta_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t delta)
set_tests_properties(time_format_delta_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  .*\n.*#2  1\\.001000  .*\n.*#3  1\\.001000  ")

# a/absolute (HH:MM:SS.ffffff) and ad/absolute-date (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff), UTC by default
# (--time-offset) -- 1700000000 is 2023-11-14 22:13:20 UTC.
add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_utc_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t absolute)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_utc_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  22:13:20\\.000000Z  ")

add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_date_utc_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t ad)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_date_utc_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  2023-11-14 22:13:20\\.000000Z  ")

# --time-offset with a fixed "+HH:MM" shifts absolute/absolute-date's rendered wall-clock time and
# suffix; +02:00 turns 22:13:20 UTC into 00:13:20 the next calendar day.
add_test(NAME time_format_absolute_date_fixed_offset_text
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t ad --time-offset +02:00)
set_tests_properties(time_format_absolute_date_fixed_offset_text PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  2023-11-15 00:13:20\\.000000\\+02:00  ")

# --time-offset is meaningless for relative/delta/epoch (only absolute/absolute-date consult it)
# -- given anyway, it's silently ignored rather than rejected, since the flags are independent and
# nothing about the combination is actually invalid.
add_test(NAME time_offset_ignored_for_relative
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t relative --time-offset +02:00)
set_tests_properties(time_offset_ignored_for_relative PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  ")

# An unrecognized -t value is rejected at CLI-parse time (CLI::IsMember), same convention as
# --format's own bad-value handling.
add_test(NAME time_format_bad_value_rejected
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --format text -t bogus)
set_tests_properties(time_format_bad_value_rejected PROPERTIES
  WILL_FAIL TRUE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# --summarize-unclassified (policy_engine.cpp's summarize_unclassified_flows/
# write_unclassified_flow_group_summarized_text) -- added after a real, busy capture produced a
# 37MB/567K-line text report, almost entirely from UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC entries for host pairs
# reconnecting thousands of times (a new TCP flow, and so a new report entry, on every reconnect).
# tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_summarize_unclassified_sample) has three flow patterns: A (3 flows, same client/server/
# port, both zone-classified -- the "no recognized protocol" unclassified reason), B (2 flows, same
# client/server as A but a DIFFERENT port, proving the grouping key includes port), and C (2 flows,
# to an address outside every declared zone -- the OTHER unclassified reason, "no declared zone
# contains ..."). See tests/policies/summarize_unclassified.yaml's own header comment for the zones.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_off_by_default
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml")
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_off_by_default PROPERTIES
  # Without the flag, all 7 flows are still listed individually -- proves the flag is opt-in and
  # nothing about the default report changed by adding this feature.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC \\(7\\):\n(  \\[[0-9]+\\].*\n)+"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "summarized into")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_collapses_into_three_groups
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_collapses_into_three_groups PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC \\(7 flow\\(s\\), summarized into 3 distinct pattern\\(s\\)")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_a_flow_and_packet_counts
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_a_flow_and_packet_counts PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:9999  -- 3 flow\\(s\\), 6 packet\\(s\\) total\n *zones: hmi_zone -> plc_zone\n *mac: [0-9a-f:]+ -> [0-9a-f:]+\n *no recognized OT protocol traffic was found on any of these flows")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_b_kept_separate_by_port
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_b_kept_separate_by_port PROPERTIES
  # Same client/server IPs as pattern A, but port 8888 not 9999 -- must be its own group (2 flows,
  # 4 packets), not folded into pattern A's.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:8888  -- 2 flow\\(s\\), 4 packet\\(s\\) total")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_pattern_c_zone_reason_reused
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_pattern_c_zone_reason_reused PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50 -> 10\\.0\\.0\\.5:7777  -- 2 flow\\(s\\), 4 packet\\(s\\) total\n *zones: hmi_zone -> unclassified\n *mac: [0-9a-f:]+ -> [0-9a-f:]+\n *no declared zone contains 10\\.0\\.0\\.5")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_does_not_affect_violations_or_allowed
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/wrong_port.yaml" --summarize-unclassified)
set_tests_properties(summarize_unclassified_does_not_affect_violations_or_allowed PROPERTIES
  # This fixture/policy combination has 1 violation and 0 unclassified flows (see
  # policy_wrong_port_is_a_violation above) -- VIOLATIONS renders exactly as it always does,
  # completely unaffected by this flag, which only ever changes the UNCLASSIFIED TRAFFIC section.
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Result: NON-COMPLIANT \\(1 violation\\(s\\), 0 unclassified flow\\(s\\)\\).*a conduit exists between zone 'hmi_zone' and zone 'plc_zone', but none permits modbus traffic on port 502")

add_test(NAME summarize_unclassified_ignored_by_json_format
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_summarize_unclassified.pcap" --policy "${POLICY_DIR}/summarize_unclassified.yaml" --format json --summarize-unclassified)
