add_test(NAME inventory_notable_protocols_json_eapol_mac_pair
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_enterprise_trust.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_notable_protocols_json_eapol_mac_pair PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"protocol\": \"eapol\",\n      \"tier\": \"enterprise-trust\",\n      \"mac_a\": \"00:0c:29:11:22:33\",\n      \"mac_b\": \"01:80:c2:00:00:03\"")

# Regression guard, inventory side: a fixture with only ordinary (ten-protocol) OT traffic still
# reports an empty notable_protocols array, and skipped_packets is unaffected by this feature --
# same pairing as notable_protocols_empty_for_ordinary_ot_traffic above, for `inventory`.
add_test(NAME inventory_notable_protocols_empty_for_ordinary_ot_traffic
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(inventory_notable_protocols_empty_for_ordinary_ot_traffic PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"skipped_packets\": 0,.*\"notable_protocols\": \\[.*\\]")

# ============================================================================================
# CLI-configurable resource-exhaustion limits (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's "External code review and
# engineering priorities" item 7 -- see resource_limits.hpp for the full design). Five grouped
# `--max-*` flags, each overriding a whole category of the ~60-odd individually-named DoS-
# protection constants scattered across decoder.cpp and the protocol files. 0/unset (never
# passed) means every site keeps its own compile-time default -- already proven byte-identical
# to this feature's absence by the fact that every other test in this file above, none of which
# passes any of these five flags, still passes unchanged. The tests below instead demonstrate
# each flag's actual effect: set low enough, it visibly and correctly changes decode behavior.
# ============================================================================================

# --max-reassembly-bytes: sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap's first split (Modbus/TCP, 29 bytes across
# 2 TCP segments) normally reassembles cleanly (see tcp_reassembly_completes_and_decodes below/
# above); set low enough, decoder.cpp's general TCP reassembly path now abandons it instead.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-bytes 5 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_bytes_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment reassembly on this flow exceeded its safety cap \\(29 byte\\(s\\) across 2 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it; this segment's own payload is tried fresh instead")

# --max-reassembly-segments: same fixture/flow, same effect via the segment-count half of the
# same cap instead of the byte-count half -- confirms both halves of decoder.cpp's `if` are
# independently reachable through their own flag.
add_test(NAME max_reassembly_segments_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_tcp_reassembly.pcap" --format text --max-reassembly-segments 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_reassembly_segments_abandons_normally_successful_reassembly PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "TCP segment reassembly on this flow exceeded its safety cap \\(29 byte\\(s\\) across 2 segment\\(s\\)\\) -- abandoning it; this segment's own payload is tried fresh instead")

# --max-recursion-depth: tests/sample_goose_deep_nesting.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own
# build_goose_deep_nesting_sample -- see its docstring) is a GOOSE allData structure nested three
# levels deep specifically so this flag has something to truncate; every other GOOSE fixture's
# allData is at most one level deep, too shallow to demonstrate this flag at any CLI-
# representable value (0 means "unset/default", not "a cap of zero").
add_test(NAME max_recursion_depth_goose_truncates
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_goose_deep_nesting.pcap" --format text --max-recursion-depth 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_recursion_depth_goose_truncates PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: allData\\[0.0\\]: nesting exceeds max depth \\(1\\) -- not decoded further")

# --max-decoded-objects: sample_dnp3.pcap's first Response frame carries two object headers
# (g1v2 with 3 points, g30v1) -- set low enough, both dnp3.cpp's per-fragment object-header cap
# and its per-header point-value cap visibly truncate, in the same decoded frame.
add_test(NAME max_decoded_objects_dnp3_truncates_headers_and_points
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_dnp3.pcap" --format text --max-decoded-objects 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_decoded_objects_dnp3_truncates_headers_and_points PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "objects: \\[g1v2\\][^\n]*\n *note: object header 0: only the first 1 of 3 point value\\(s\\) were decoded \\(safety cap\\)[^\n]*\n *note: stopped after 1 object header\\(s\\), more may remain \\(safety cap\\)")

# --max-coalesced-messages: sample_hartip.pcap's Keep Alive flow normally decodes 2 HART-IP
# messages coalesced in one TCP payload (see hartip_tcp_coalesced_keep_alive_decoded above);
# set to 1, only the first is decoded and the existing "stopped after N" note style fires at the
# configured N instead of the compile-time default.
add_test(NAME max_coalesced_messages_hartip_stops_at_one
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_hartip.pcap" --format text --max-coalesced-messages 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_coalesced_messages_hartip_stops_at_one PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192.168.1.50:52150 -> 192.168.1.10:5094 \\(hart-ip\\)  \\[hartip\\]  Request Keep Alive[^\n]*\n *note: stopped after 1 HART-IP message\\(s\\) in this one TCP payload, more may remain \\(safety cap\\)")

# All seven flags are registered identically on all three subcommands (unlike the --modbus-port-
# style port-list flags, which remain decode-only) -- confirmed here via --help rather than only
# by cli_main.cpp's own add_resource_limit_options call sites, so a future accidental removal
# from one subcommand's wiring is actually caught by the test suite.
add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_decode_help
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_decode_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries")

add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_policy_validate_help
  COMMAND conduitscope policy validate --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_policy_validate_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries")

add_test(NAME resource_limit_flags_present_in_inventory_help
  COMMAND conduitscope inventory --help)
set_tests_properties(resource_limit_flags_present_in_inventory_help PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "--max-reassembly-bytes[^\n]*\n.*--max-reassembly-segments[^\n]*\n.*--max-recursion-depth[^\n]*\n.*--max-decoded-objects[^\n]*\n.*--max-coalesced-messages[^\n]*\n.*--max-active-flows[^\n]*\n.*--max-flow-state-entries")

# ============================================================================================
# --max-active-flows / --max-flow-state-entries (docs/reviews/2026-09-chatgpt-security-review-
# patch160.md finding 1: "Unbounded lifetime of TCP/decoder flow state"). A different category
# from the five flags above: those bound the COST of any one flow/reassembly/message; these two
# bound the COUNT of distinct flows/sessions tracked at once, regardless of a capture's total
# flow count. See resource_limits.hpp's own comments on both fields and
# Decoder::reassemble_tcp_payload's/DecodeContext::flow_state<T>()'s (protocol_decoder.hpp) own
# fix comments for the full rationale.
# ============================================================================================

# --max-active-flows: sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's
# build_resource_exhaustion_active_flows_sample) has two DISTINCT TCP flows, each left "waiting
# for more" mid-reassembly. Uncapped, both entries coexist in Decoder::tcp_reassembly_ with no
# interaction; capped to 1, the second flow's own still-incomplete segment must evict the first
# flow's entry to make room.
add_test(NAME max_active_flows_evicts_other_flow_entry
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap" --format text --max-active-flows 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_active_flows_evicts_other_flow_entry PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2[^\n]*51701[^\n]*waiting for more[^\n]*\n *note: active TCP flow-reassembly limit \\(1\\) reached -- evicted an existing in-progress reassembly on another flow to make room for this one \\(--max-active-flows\\)")

# Unset (the default): both flows' entries coexist, no eviction note anywhere -- byte-identical
# to this feature's absence, the same bar every other resource_limits() field is held to.
add_test(NAME max_active_flows_unset_no_eviction
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_active_flows.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_active_flows_unset_no_eviction PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "waiting for more"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "active TCP flow-reassembly limit")

# --max-flow-state-entries: sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap (build_resource_
# exhaustion_flow_state_sample) has two DISTINCT Modbus TCP sessions, each opening with a
# request (creating a ModbusFlowState entry in Decoder::registry_flow_state_). Capped to 1,
# session 2's own request must evict session 1's entry; session 1's later response (matching
# transaction id, same session) then finds no pending request -- modbus.cpp's own "no
# outstanding request found" note -- proving the eviction actually happened, not merely that the
# flag was accepted. Contrast with modbus_authoritative_transaction_pairing-style tests
# elsewhere in this file, which show the SAME response correctly paired when nothing evicted it.
add_test(NAME max_flow_state_entries_evicts_other_session_state
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --format text --max-flow-state-entries 1 --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_flow_state_entries_evicts_other_session_state PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: no outstanding request found on this TCP session for transaction id 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing")

# Unset (the default): session 1's response still pairs authoritatively -- byte-identical to
# this feature's absence.
add_test(NAME max_flow_state_entries_unset_still_pairs
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_resource_exhaustion_flow_state.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(max_flow_state_entries_unset_still_pairs PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 100"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "no outstanding request found")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ARP (RFC 826, EtherType 0x0806, arp.hpp) -- Stage 2 new-protocol work, not a migration (see
# decoder.hpp's own comment on ProtocolFilter::ArpOnly). tests/sample_arp.pcap
# (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own build_arp_sample) covers an ARP Request, an ARP Reply, a
# gratuitous ARP (Reply with SPA==TPA), an ARP Probe (RFC 5227), an ARP Announcement (RFC 5227,
# wire-identical to a gratuitous Request, so both notes fire), and a non-Ethernet/non-IPv4 HTYPE
# case (HTYPE=6, raw-hex SHA/SPA/THA/TPA fallback). NOT to be confused with
# tests/sample_link_transport_layers.pcap's own ARP frame (link_layer_arp_ethertype_named above)
# -- that one's OPER reads as 0x0000, an unrecognized opcode, so try_parse_arp's own structural
# gate declines it and it correctly stays "[non-ip]"; the two fixtures are deliberately
# independent and neither one's coverage substitutes for the other's.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_test(NAME arp_request_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(arp_request_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Request -- who has 192\\.168\\.1\\.10\\? tell 192\\.168\\.1\\.50 \\(00:0c:29:11:22:33\\)")

add_test(NAME arp_reply_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(arp_reply_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Reply -- 192\\.168\\.1\\.10 is at 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc\n")

add_test(NAME arp_gratuitous_reply_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(arp_gratuitous_reply_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Reply -- 192\\.168\\.1\\.10 is at 00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\[gratuitous\\]\n *note: Gratuitous ARP \\(sender and target protocol address match\\)")

add_test(NAME arp_probe_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(arp_probe_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Request -- who has 192\\.168\\.1\\.99\\? tell 0\\.0\\.0\\.0 \\(00:0c:29:de:ad:99\\) \\[probe\\]\n *note: ARP Probe \\(RFC 5227\\): sender protocol address is 0\\.0\\.0\\.0")

add_test(NAME arp_announcement_decoded_with_both_notes
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(arp_announcement_decoded_with_both_notes PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Request -- who has 192\\.168\\.1\\.99\\? tell 192\\.168\\.1\\.99 \\(00:0c:29:de:ad:99\\) \\[announcement\\]\n *note: Gratuitous ARP \\(sender and target protocol address match\\)[^\n]*\n *note: ARP Announcement \\(RFC 5227\\): sender and target protocol address both name the newly-claimed address")

# HTYPE=6 ("IEEE 802 Networks") is not HTYPE==1 (Ethernet), so is_ethernet_ipv4 stays false
# despite PTYPE==0x0800 (still named "IPv4") -- SHA/SPA/THA/TPA are shown as raw hex (via the
# parenthetical htype/ptype/hlen/plen summary), never guessed at as a MAC/dotted-quad, per
# arp.hpp's own "structural detection gate"/is_ethernet_ipv4 comment.
add_test(NAME arp_non_ethernet_htype_raw_hex_fallback
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(arp_non_ethernet_htype_raw_hex_fallback PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\]  ARP Reply \\(htype=6, ptype=0x800 \\(IPv4\\), hlen=6, plen=4\\)")

# --protocol arp isolation: every one of the six frames in sample_arp.pcap must still decode as
# arp (ArpOnly is EtherType-gated same as Auto mode here, no port to restrict), and none may fall
# through to "non-ip"/"parse-error" -- confirms ProtocolFilter::ArpOnly's own decoder.cpp wiring
# doesn't accidentally decline a frame Auto mode would otherwise accept.
add_test(NAME arp_protocol_filter_isolates_arp_only
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --protocol arp --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(arp_protocol_filter_isolates_arp_only PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\].*\\[arp\\].*\\[arp\\].*\\[arp\\].*\\[arp\\].*\\[arp\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[non-ip\\]|\\[parse-error\\]")

add_test(NAME arp_stats_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --stats --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(arp_stats_counted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: +6[^\n]*\n.*protocols:\n *arp +6")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB, EtherType 0x88CC, lldp.hpp) -- Stage 2 new-protocol work, not a migration

# A trailing TLV (after the mandatory 3, which decode fine) declares a 10-byte value but only 3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CDP (Cisco Discovery Protocol, cdp.hpp) -- roadmap item 48. Unlike ARP/LLDP above (both
# EtherType-keyed), CDP has no EtherType at all: it rides classic IEEE 802.3 LLC framing, SNAP-
# encapsulated under Cisco's own OUI (00:00:0C), keyed by its own SNAP Protocol ID (0x2000) -- the
# exact same envelope Cisco (R)PVST+ uses (see stp.hpp), disambiguated purely by that Protocol ID.
# This release also fixes a real, pre-existing collision this same envelope caused: EVERY Cisco-OUI
# SNAP frame -- CDP's own included -- used to be unconditionally reported as "Cisco PVST+ (SNAP-
# encapsulated, not decoded)" regardless of its actual SNAP Protocol ID. Verified as a real,
# reproducible mislabeling before this fix landed (see decoder.cpp's own SNAP call site comment for
# how); the cdp_pinning_* tests below keep that pre-fix behavior pinned against regression by
# asserting it still occurs for genuinely-PVST+-PID (0x010B) traffic, and asserting it no longer
# occurs for CDP's own PID (0x2000). tests/sample_cdp.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's own
# build_cdp_sample) covers: a full-field CDPv2 announcement (Device ID, Addresses with a real IPv4,
# Port ID, Capabilities, Software Version, Platform, Native VLAN, Duplex, VTP Management Domain,
# System Name, Management Address, Power Consumption/Requested/Available); a minimal CDPv1 frame; an
# HP-proprietary-range unknown TLV (structural-only fallback); a frame too short even for the 4-byte
# header (CDP-but-truncated, not generic-SNAP); a frame with an in-body TLV-length overrun (tolerant
# truncation, not a whole-frame decline); the two pinning-collision fixtures (CDP-shaped PID 0x2000,
# and PVST+-shaped PID 0x010B); a third, unrelated Cisco-OUI SNAP Protocol ID (VTP's own 0x2003,
# proving the fix's naming is precise, not just a two-way split); and a non-Cisco-OUI negative
# control (proving no false-positive).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_test(NAME cdp_full_field_cdpv2_announcement_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cdp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(cdp_full_field_cdpv2_announcement_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[cdp\\]  CDP v2 device=\"switch-core-01.plant.local\" port=\"GigabitEthernet0/1\" platform=\"cisco WS-C2960-24TT-L\" addr=192.168.1.50")

add_test(NAME cdp_full_field_json_fields
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cdp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(cdp_full_field_json_fields PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"cdp_version\": 2,\n *\"cdp_ttl_seconds\": 180,\n *\"cdp_device_id\": \"switch-core-01.plant.local\",\n *\"cdp_port_id\": \"GigabitEthernet0/1\",\n *\"cdp_platform\": \"cisco WS-C2960-24TT-L\",\n *\"cdp_software_version\": \"Cisco IOS Software, C2960 Software, Version 15.2\\(2\\)E\",\n *\"cdp_capabilities\": 24,\n *\"cdp_capabilities_names\": \\[\"Switch\", \"Host\"\\],\n *\"cdp_native_vlan\": 100,\n *\"cdp_duplex\": \"Full\",\n *\"cdp_vtp_management_domain\": \"PLANT-VTP-DOMAIN\",\n *\"cdp_system_name\": \"switch-core-01\",\n *\"cdp_power_consumption_mw\": 7000,\n *\"cdp_power_requested_mw\": 15400,\n *\"cdp_power_available_mw\": 30800,\n *\"cdp_addresses\": \\[\\{\"protocol_type\": \"NLPID\", \"protocol\": \"IP\", \"is_ipv4\": true, \"address\": \"192.168.1.50\"\\}\\],\n *\"cdp_management_addresses\": \\[\\{\"protocol_type\": \"NLPID\", \"protocol\": \"IP\", \"is_ipv4\": true, \"address\": \"192.168.1.1\"\\}\\]")

add_test(NAME cdp_minimal_cdpv1_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cdp.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[cdp\\]  CDP v1 device=\"router-edge-01\" port=\"Ethernet0/0\" platform=\"cisco 2621XM\"")

add_test(NAME cdp_unknown_vendor_tlv_structural_fallback

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"type\": 4101, \"type_name\": \"HP-proprietary extension\", \"length\": 8, \"raw_hex\": \"0xdeadbeef\"")

# Too short even for the fixed 4-byte header -- try_parse_cdp declines entirely; decoder.cpp names
# this as CDP-but-truncated (the SNAP Protocol ID already confirms it WAS meant to be CDP) rather

# Pinning-collision fixture A: a CDP-shaped SNAP frame (SNAP Protocol ID 0x2000) now decodes as
# "cdp", NOT "Cisco PVST+ (SNAP-encapsulated, not decoded)" -- the mislabeling this release's own
# roadmap item 48 fixed (see this section's own header comment above).
add_test(NAME cdp_pinning_cdp_pid_decodes_as_cdp_not_pvst
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cdp.pcap")

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[cdp\\]  CDP v2 device=\"pinning-fixture-cdp\" port=\"Gi0/2\"")

# Pinning-collision fixture B: the byte-for-byte same frame, but with PVST+'s own genuine SNAP
# Protocol ID (0x010B) instead of CDP's -- must still decode as "Cisco PVST+ (SNAP-encapsulated,
# not decoded)", confirming the fix didn't overcorrect into calling every Cisco-OUI SNAP frame "cdp".

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[non-ip\\]  Cisco PVST\\+ \\(SNAP-encapsulated, not decoded\\)")

# A third Cisco-OUI SNAP Protocol ID (VTP's own real PID, 0x2003) that is neither CDP's nor PVST+'s
# -- must be named generically, proving this fix's own naming is precise (a real 3-way split), not
# just a CDP-vs-everything-else binary.
add_test(NAME cdp_other_cisco_snap_pid_named_generically
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cdp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(cdp_other_cisco_snap_pid_named_generically PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[non-ip\\]  Cisco SNAP frame \\(OUI=00:00:0C, ProtocolID=0x2003, not decoded\\)")

# Negative control: a non-Cisco SNAP OUI (00:00:5E) under the exact same SNAP Protocol ID value CDP
# uses (0x2000) -- must NOT decode as "cdp" (detection keys on SNAP_OUI_CISCO too, not the PID alone).

# --protocol cdp isolation: every CDP-PID SNAP frame in sample_cdp.pcap must still decode as cdp
# (CdpOnly gates the same SNAP-OUI+PID structural check Auto mode uses here, no port to restrict);
# every non-CDP frame (truncated CDP, PVST+, other Cisco SNAP PID, non-Cisco OUI) still falls

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[parse-error\\]")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# BGP-4 (RFC 4271, TCP port 179, bgp.hpp) -- the last piece of the three-stage plan that also
# added ARP and LLDP. Unlike those two, BGP is TCP-port-independent and needs declared-length TCP
# reassembly, a message-coalescing loop, and session-scoped state (BgpFlowState) -- see bgp.hpp's
# own file header comment for the full wire format and docs/PROTOCOL_COVERAGE.md for the audit
# framing. Fixture generated by tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_bgp_sample -- tests/sample_bgp.pcap
# (10 packets: an OPEN exchange between two peers -- one 4-octet-AS capable, one not -- an UPDATE
# with ORIGIN/AS_PATH/NEXT_HOP/COMMUNITY/MP_REACH_NLRI, a pure-withdrawal UPDATE, 3 KEEPALIVEs
# coalesced into one TCP segment, an RFC 8203 shutdown NOTIFICATION, one UPDATE split across two
# TCP segments, a ROUTE-REFRESH on a non-standard port, and a non-BGP-shaped negative control on
# BGP's own standard port).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME bgp_open_exchange_four_octet_as_capability_asymmetric
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bgp.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(bgp_open_exchange_four_octet_as_capability_asymmetric PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[bgp\\]  BGP OPEN version=4 my_as=23456 hold_time=180 identifier=10\\.0\\.0\\.1 \\[4-octet-AS capable\\].*\\[bgp\\]  BGP OPEN version=4 my_as=65002 hold_time=180 identifier=10\\.0\\.0\\.2  \\(client")

# Peer B's OPEN (no 4-octet AS capability) was processed second on this same session, so
# BgpFlowState's own AS-number width is authoritatively 2-byte by the time the later UPDATE's
# AS_PATH attribute is decoded -- confirmed via the JSON-only "authoritative" field (see
# bgp.hpp's own AS_PATH paragraph for exactly why this is session-scoped, not per-direction).
add_test(NAME bgp_as_path_authoritative_two_byte_width_after_non_capable_open
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bgp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(bgp_as_path_authoritative_two_byte_width_after_non_capable_open PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bgp_update_as_path\": \"65001 65002 65003\",\n *\"bgp_update_as_path_authoritative\": true")

add_test(NAME bgp_update_origin_as_path_next_hop_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bgp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(bgp_update_origin_as_path_next_hop_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[bgp\\]  BGP UPDATE withdrawn=0 nlri=0 attrs=5 as_path=\\[65001 65002 65003\\] next_hop=10\\.0\\.0\\.1")

# COMMUNITY (a recognized well-known value plus an uncurated raw-hex one) and MP_REACH_NLRI
# (AFI=1/SAFI=1, next hop, two IPv4 NLRI prefixes) -- both only surfaced in full by JSON's own
# bgp_update_path_attributes array (see output.cpp's write_bgp_json_fields).
add_test(NAME bgp_update_communities_and_mp_reach_nlri_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bgp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(bgp_update_communities_and_mp_reach_nlri_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"COMMUNITY: NO_EXPORT, 0x1E0064\".*\"MP_REACH_NLRI: AFI=1 SAFI=1 nexthop=10\\.0\\.0\\.1 nlri=\\[203\\.0\\.113\\.0/24, 198\\.51\\.0\\.0/16\\]\"")

add_test(NAME bgp_update_withdrawn_routes_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_bgp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(bgp_update_withdrawn_routes_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[bgp\\]  BGP UPDATE withdrawn=2 nlri=0 attrs=0")

add_test(NAME bgp_update_withdrawn_routes_prefixes_in_json

set_tests_properties(bgp_update_withdrawn_routes_prefixes_in_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"bgp_update_withdrawn_routes\": \\[\"203\\.0\\.113\\.0/24\", \"203\\.0\\.114\\.0/24\"\\]")

# Three KEEPALIVEs coalesced into a single TCP segment -- exercises BgpDecoder::decode's own
# coalescing loop (see bgp.hpp/bgp.cpp).
add_test(NAME bgp_coalesced_keepalives_in_one_tcp_segment

# RFC 8203 shutdown communication (Cease/Administrative Shutdown).

# One UPDATE split across two TCP segments, the split point deliberately after the complete
# 19-byte header (not mid-header, see build_bgp_sample's own comment on why) -- exercises

# A ROUTE-REFRESH on a non-standard BGP port (1179, not 179) -- BGP's own detection gate is

# --bgp-port 1179 suppresses that same note (mirrors Modbus's/TwinCAT's own --*-port precedent).
add_test(NAME bgp_extra_port_flag_suppresses_non_standard_port_note

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10:55000 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.50:1179  \\[bgp\\]  BGP ROUTE-REFRESH AFI=1 SAFI=1  \\(client"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard BGP port")

# Negative control: a TCP/179 payload whose leading 16 bytes are NOT all 0xFF -- BGP's own Marker

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.10:56000 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.50:179  \\[bgp\\]")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IEEE 802.3 "Slow Protocols" (EtherType 0x8809, slow_protocols.hpp) -- added right after the
# three-stage ARP/LLDP/BGP plan, at Jurgen's request. One EtherType, Subtype-multiplexed into
# three genuinely distinct link-layer control protocols (see slow_protocols.hpp's own file header
# comment): LACP (subtype 0x01), Marker Protocol (subtype 0x02), and 802.3 OAM/EFM (subtype
# 0x03). Like TwinCAT/BGP (and unlike ARP/LLDP's own flat dual-write), the decoded message is
# carried whole in out.result and rendered via JsonWriter's own write_slow_protocols_json_fields
# (output.cpp) -- OAM's sub-message nests too deeply for a flat dual-write. Fixture generated by
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_slow_protocols_sample -- tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap (9
# packets: a well-formed LACPDU with Actor and Partner both fully in sync, the same LACPDU with
# the Actor's Synchronization bit cleared (Out of Sync note), a negative control with a corrupted
# Actor Information TLV length (falls back to "[non-ip]"), a Marker Information (request), a
# Marker Response Information (echoing the same requester fields back), an OAM Information OAMPDU
# with the Dying Gasp flag set and both a Local (Mode Active) and Remote (Mode Passive)
# Information TLV, an OAM Event Notification OAMPDU with one Errored Frame Event, an OAM Loopback
# Control OAMPDU requesting Enable, and a second negative control -- an unsupported Subtype
# (0x0A, ESMC/G.8264) that also falls back to "[non-ip]").
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_lacp_in_sync_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_lacp_in_sync_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\]  LACP actor=00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(key=1 port=1 pri=32768\\) partner=00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(key=1 port=1 pri=32768\\) \\[Activity=Active Timeout=Short Aggregation=Aggregatable Synchronization=InSync Collecting=Enabled Distributing=Enabled Defaulted=No Expired=No\\]")

# The Actor's own Synchronization bit (0x08) is cleared on this second LACPDU -- Partner stays in
# sync -- exercising the "LACP Out of Sync reported" note (fires when either side is Out of Sync).
add_test(NAME slow_protocols_lacp_out_of_sync_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap" --verbose)
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_lacp_out_of_sync_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\]  LACP actor=00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc \\(key=1 port=1 pri=32768\\) partner=00:0c:29:11:22:33 \\(key=1 port=1 pri=32768\\) \\[Activity=Active Timeout=Short Aggregation=Aggregatable Synchronization=OutOfSync Collecting=Enabled Distributing=Enabled Defaulted=No Expired=No\\]\n *note: LACP Out of Sync reported")

# Negative control: the Actor Information TLV's own declared Length is 19, not the fixed 20 --
# breaks parse_lacp's structural gate (every TLV's type+length must match exactly), so this must
# fall through to the generic ethertype-name "[non-ip]" fallback, NOT "[slow-protocols]" -- the
# equivalent of ARP's/LLDP's own unknown-opcode/wrong-order negative-control coverage.
add_test(NAME slow_protocols_lacp_corrupted_length_falls_back_to_non_ip
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_lacp_corrupted_length_falls_back_to_non_ip PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  2\\.002000.*\\[non-ip\\]  Ethernet frame with ethertype 0x8809 \\(IEEE 802\\.3 Slow Protocols \\(LACP/Marker/OAM\\)\\) \\(not IPv4\\)")

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_marker_information_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_marker_information_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\]  Marker Information requester=00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc port=5 transaction_id=3735928559")

# Marker Response Information echoes the same requester fields back, as a real Marker Responder
# does -- distinguished from the request above only by the "Response" word (is_response=true).
add_test(NAME slow_protocols_marker_response_information_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_marker_response_information_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\]  Marker Response Information requester=00:0c:29:aa:bb:cc port=5 transaction_id=3735928559")

# Local Information TLV (Mode Active, all four capability bits set, OUI 00:0c:29) and Remote
# Information TLV (Mode Passive, no capability bits set, OUI 00:0c:30) -- both only surfaced in
# full by JSON's own write_slow_protocols_json_fields (output.cpp).
add_test(NAME slow_protocols_oam_information_local_remote_fields_json

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_oam_dying_gasp_note

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\]  OAM Information local=Local Info: version=1 mode=Active oui=00:0c:29 remote=Remote Info: version=1 mode=Passive oui=00:0c:30\n *note: OAM Dying Gasp flag set")

# One Errored Frame Event (type 0x02): window=1000 threshold=10 errors=15

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_oam_loopback_control_enable_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_oam_loopback_control_enable_decoded PROPERTIES

# Negative control: unsupported subtype 0x0A (ESMC/G.8264) -- try_parse_slow_protocols declines

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_stats_counted
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format text --stats --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_slow_protocols.pcap")
set_tests_properties(slow_protocols_stats_counted PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "packets: +9[^\n]*\n.*protocols:\n *non-ip +2\n *slow-protocols +7")

# --protocol slow-protocols isolation: every one of the seven decodable frames in
# sample_slow_protocols.pcap must still decode as slow-protocols (SlowProtocolsOnly is
# EtherType-gated same as Auto mode here, no port to restrict); the two structurally-declined
# frames (corrupted LACPDU length, unsupported subtype) still fall through to "[non-ip]" even
# under this filter -- the same posture ArpOnly's/LldpOnly's own isolation tests already
# established -- and neither one is ever mis-tagged "[slow-protocols]" nor crashes into
# "[parse-error]".

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[non-ip\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[slow-protocols\\].*\\[non-ip\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[parse-error\\]")

add_test(NAME slow_protocols_protocol_filter_excludes_other_protocols

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[modbus\\]")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WinRM (WS-Management), TCP port 5985 -- see winrm.hpp's own extensive file header comment for
# the wire format. tests/sample_winrm.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_winrm_sample()) has
# 19 packets: a full Create->Command->Send->Receive->Signal->Delete shell session on one real TCP
# stream (#1-#12), then, each its own TCP flow: a CIM/WQL Enumerate (#13), a PSRP Create (#14), a
# Basic-auth Command (#15), a chunked-encoding negative case (#16), a SOAP Fault response (#17), a
# 401 Unauthorized response (#18), and the same Create request as #1 on a non-standard port 8585
# (#19). tests/sample_winrm_tcp_split.pcap has a separate 2-packet fixture: the same Command
# request shape as #3's, split mid-header-block across two TCP segments.

add_test(NAME winrm_create_response_shell_opened_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format text --verbose)
set_tests_properties(winrm_create_response_shell_opened_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2  1\\.001000.*\\[winrm\\]  HTTP/1\\.1 200 OK -- WS-Man CreateResponse.*note: remote shell opened \\(ShellId AAAAAAAA-1111-2222-3333-444444444444\\)")

# Negative control: the Create REQUEST (#1) must NOT carry the "remote shell opened" note (only a
# successful response actually proves a shell exists) -- and, since the shell doesn't exist yet
# when this request is sent, its JSON has no winrm_shell_id field at all.
add_test(NAME winrm_create_request_no_premature_shell_opened_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_create_request_no_premature_shell_opened_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"Create\",\n    \"winrm_resource_uri\": \"http://schemas\\.microsoft\\.com/wbem/wsman/1/windows/shell/cmd\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"Create\",\n    \"winrm_resource_uri\"[^}]*\"winrm_shell_id\"")

# Command request (#3): "command executed" note fires, and both the note text and the
# winrm_command_line field are redacted by default (DecodeContext::redact_secrets).
add_test(NAME winrm_command_executed_redacted_by_default
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_command_executed_redacted_by_default PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"Command\",.*\"winrm_shell_id\": \"AAAAAAAA-1111-2222-3333-444444444444\",\n    \"winrm_command_line\": \"\\[REDACTED\\]\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\"command executed: \\[REDACTED\\]\"\\]")

# --no-redact reveals the real command text for the same packet.
add_test(NAME winrm_command_line_visible_with_no_redact
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json --no-redact)
set_tests_properties(winrm_command_line_visible_with_no_redact PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"Command\",.*\"winrm_command_line\": \"cmd\\.exe /c whoami /all\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\"command executed: cmd\\.exe /c whoami /all\"\\]")

# Negative control: the Command RESPONSE (#4) must NOT carry "command executed" (the command text
# only ever lives on the wire in the request; the response only ever carries a CommandId) -- and
# its CommandId is extracted via the element-text wire shape (<rsp:CommandId>...</rsp:CommandId>).
add_test(NAME winrm_command_response_command_id_element_text_shape_no_premature_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_command_response_command_id_element_text_shape_no_premature_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"CommandResponse\",.*\"winrm_command_id\": \"7777AAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD-888888888888\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\\]")

# Send request (#5): CommandId extracted via the XML-ATTRIBUTE wire shape instead (the REQUEST-side
# shape every later Send/Receive/Signal carries it in) -- a genuinely different shape from the
# Command response's own element-text form above, both must resolve to the identical CommandId.
add_test(NAME winrm_send_request_command_id_attribute_shape
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_send_request_command_id_attribute_shape PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"Send\",.*\"winrm_shell_id\": \"AAAAAAAA-1111-2222-3333-444444444444\",\n    \"winrm_command_id\": \"7777AAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD-888888888888\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\\]")

# Receive response (#8): proves find_start_tag's own exact-tag-boundary check keeps "CommandState"
# (and the CommandId/Stream attributes riding alongside it) from ever false-matching a "Command"
# element search -- CommandId still resolves via the attribute-anywhere fallback, but no
# winrm_command_line field is ever produced for this response (there is no Command element in a
# ReceiveResponse body at all).
add_test(NAME winrm_receive_response_command_state_not_misparsed_as_command
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_receive_response_command_state_not_misparsed_as_command PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_action_name\": \"ReceiveResponse\",.*\"winrm_command_id\": \"7777AAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD-888888888888\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\\]")

# Delete request/response (#11/#12) close the shell -- plain structural coverage, no notes.
add_test(NAME winrm_delete_request_and_response_decoded
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(winrm_delete_request_and_response_decoded PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[winrm\\]  POST /wsman -- WS-Man Delete.*\\[winrm\\]  HTTP/1\\.1 200 OK -- WS-Man DeleteResponse")

# CIM/WQL Enumerate (#13): is_cim_query (ResourceURI names a CIM class path) plus a WQL Filter

# HTTP Basic auth over plaintext WinRM (#15): fires alongside "command executed" (redacted) on the
# very same message -- both notes present together, proving they're independent checks.
add_test(NAME winrm_basic_auth_and_command_executed_together
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format text --verbose)

# Chunked-encoding negative case (#16): proves the documented "not reassembled" limitation behaves
# as designed -- header-only declared length (winrm_content_length is entirely absent, since
# has_content_length is never set for a chunked message), a dedicated note, and no envelope fields
# at all (has_envelope requires a body scan that chunked messages never get).
add_test(NAME winrm_chunked_body_not_reassembled
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_chunked_body_not_reassembled PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"POST /wsman \\(chunked body, not decoded\\)\",\n    \"winrm_is_response\": false,\n    \"winrm_http_method\": \"POST\",\n    \"winrm_http_target\": \"/wsman\",\n    \"winrm_content_type\": \"application/soap\\+xml;charset=UTF-8\",\n    \"winrm_chunked\": true,\n    \"notes\": \\[\n      \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked body -- this decoder does not reassemble or decode a chunked WS-Man body")

# SOAP Fault response (#17): triggers the SOAP Fault note with its own Reason/Text.
add_test(NAME winrm_soap_fault_note
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_soap_fault_note PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_http_status\": 500,\n    \"winrm_http_status_text\": \"Internal Server Error\",.*\"winrm_fault_reason\": \"Access is denied\\.\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\"WS-Man SOAP Fault: Access is denied\\.\"\\]")

# 401 Unauthorized response (#18): response-side auth-scheme coverage (WWW-Authenticate) with NO
# envelope at all -- the body is text/html, not application/soap+xml, so is_soap_xml is false and
# the body is never scanned (no winrm_action/winrm_resource_uri/etc. fields at all).
add_test(NAME winrm_401_response_auth_scheme_no_envelope
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(winrm_401_response_auth_scheme_no_envelope PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_http_status\": 401,\n    \"winrm_http_status_text\": \"Unauthorized\",\n    \"winrm_content_type\": \"text/html\",\n    \"winrm_chunked\": false,\n    \"winrm_content_length\": 38,\n    \"winrm_auth_scheme\": \"Negotiate\",\n    \"notes\": \\[\\]"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"winrm_http_status\": 401,[^}]*\"winrm_action\"")

# Non-standard port (#19), default Auto mode: WinRmTcpDecoder's own port gate correctly declines
# it -- proven by the absence of "[winrm]" for this specific flow. (What DOES claim it here is a
# genuine, pre-existing, entirely unrelated collision -- MQTT's own port-independent structural
# check reads this request's leading "PO" bytes as a plausible PUBREC fixed-header byte plus a
# single-byte remaining-length; see build_winrm_sample()'s own docstring in tools/make_sample_pcap.py
# for the full explanation. Not a WinRM regression, and not the collision winrm.hpp's own COLLISION
# SURVEY section scopes -- that one is specifically against it_protocols.cpp's generic Tier-2
# "http" fallback, which this packet never even reaches.)
add_test(NAME winrm_nonstandard_port_not_recognized_in_auto_mode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(winrm_nonstandard_port_not_recognized_in_auto_mode PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:49570 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:8585  \\[winrm\\]")

add_test(NAME winrm_nonstandard_port_claimed_by_unrelated_mqtt_collision_in_auto_mode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_winrm.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(winrm_nonstandard_port_claimed_by_unrelated_mqtt_collision_in_auto_mode PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:49570 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:8585  \\[mqtt\\]")

# --winrm-port 8585 widens Auto-mode detection so WinRmTcpDecoder claims this flow ahead of MQTT
# instead -- and, since the port is now in the configured/widened set, the "not a
# configured/standard WinRM port" note must NOT fire.
add_test(NAME winrm_port_widening_with_extra_port_flag

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:49570 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:8585  \\[winrm\\]  POST /wsman -- WS-Man Create"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard WinRM port")

# --protocol winrm claims the same flow port-independently too, but here the port genuinely isn't
# configured for this invocation, so the "not a configured/standard WinRM port" note DOES fire.

add_test(NAME winrm_protocol_filter_excludes_other_protocols
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap" --protocol winrm --format text)
set_tests_properties(winrm_protocol_filter_excludes_other_protocols PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[winrm\\]")

# Collision-pinning proof (see winrm.hpp's own COLLISION SURVEY section): it_protocols.cpp's own
# generic Tier-2 "http" recognition (try_recognize_it_lateral_movement's match_http check) would
# otherwise claim every one of this fixture's port-5985 messages -- WinRmTcpDecoder is wired ahead
# of it in decoder.cpp's TCP dispatch chain specifically so that never happens, the same
# "prove the collision existed, then fix the dispatch order" method MELSEC-before-Modbus already

# --stats action-count aggregation (WinRmMessage::wsa_action_name, requests only -- see

# DCOM activation, raw DCE/RPC over TCP/135 -- Phase 5 (the last) of the Windows RPC/remote-
# management batch, see dcom.hpp's own extensive file header comment for the wire format/scope.
# tests/sample_wmi_dcom_activation.pcap (build_wmi_dcom_activation_sample()) has 22 packets across
# four TCP flows: A (#1-#8) binds IObjectExporter alone and exercises ServerAlive2/ResolveOxid2/a
# faulted ComplexPing; B (#9-#16) binds IRemoteSCMActivator+IActivation TOGETHER on one bind PDU
# and exercises RemoteGetClassObject/RemoteCreateInstance/RemoteActivation; C (#17-#21) binds an
# unrecognized interface at context 0 (REJECTED) alongside IObjectExporter at context 1 (accepted)
# on one bind PDU, proving positional bind_ack correlation, then exercises SimplePing on the
# accepted context and an unbound-context request that must fall through gracefully; D (#22) is the
# same bind as A's on a non-standard TCP port (13135), declined in Auto mode. A separate 2-packet
# fixture, sample_wmi_dcom_activation_tcp_split.pcap, splits a bind PDU across two TCP segments.

set_tests_properties(dcom_bind_ack_confirms_binding PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#2  1\\.001000.*\\[dcom\\]  DCOM bind_ack \\(bound: IObjectExporter\\)")

# Flow C (#17/#18): a bind PDU offering an UNRECOGNIZED interface at context 0 and IObjectExporter
# at context 1, whose bind_ack REJECTS position 0 and ACCEPTS position 1 -- proves bind_ack's own
# positional (not context_id-keyed) correlation attributes acceptance to the right context_id even

  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_wmi_dcom_activation.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(dcom_positional_bind_ack_skips_rejected_unrecognized_context PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#17 .*\\[dcom\\]  DCOM bind \\(candidates: IObjectExporter\\).*#18 .*\\[dcom\\]  DCOM bind_ack \\(bound: IObjectExporter\\)")

# SimplePing (#19) on context 1 -- the accepted position from the bind above -- decodes normally.
add_test(NAME dcom_simpleping_on_accepted_context_after_rejection
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_wmi_dcom_activation.pcap" --format json)

  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"summary\": \"IObjectExporter SimplePing request\",\n    \"dcom_calls\": \\[\n      \\{\n        \"interface\": \"IObjectExporter\",\n        \"opnum\": \"SimplePing\",\n        \"call_id\": 301,\n        \"context_id\": 1")

# A request on context 0 (#21) -- never bound to any known interface at all (neither recognized

# Non-standard port (#22), default Auto mode: DcomTcpDecoder's own port gate correctly declines it
# -- unlike WinRM, there's no pre-existing recognizer racing to claim it instead (see dcom.hpp's
# own COLLISION SURVEY section), so it simply falls through to generic "[tcp]".
add_test(NAME dcom_nonstandard_port_not_recognized_in_auto_mode
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_wmi_dcom_activation.pcap" --format text)

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "192\\.168\\.1\\.50:50500 -> 192\\.168\\.1\\.10:13135  \\[dcom\\]")

# --dcom-port 13135 widens Auto-mode detection so DcomTcpDecoder claims this flow -- and, since the
# port is now in the configured/widened set, the "not a configured/standard DCOM port" note must
# NOT fire.
add_test(NAME dcom_port_widening_with_extra_port_flag

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "not a configured/standard DCOM port")

# --protocol dcom claims the same flow port-independently too, but here the port genuinely isn't

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tshark-style CLI: -T fields/-e (field selection), -f/-c/-a (short aliases for --filter/
# --max-packets/--duration), -w (raw pcap capture-to-file), -x (hex+ASCII dump). See
# cli_main.cpp's own run_decode comment for the design rationale (mirrors tshark's own flags
# throughout) and output.hpp/output.cpp for FieldsWriter/write_hex_ascii_dump, pcap_writer.hpp/
# pcap_writer.cpp for PcapWriter. -f/--filter's own dedicated alias test
# (bpf_filter_dash_f_alias_narrows_correctly) lives up in the CONDUITSCOPE_HAVE_PCAP-guarded
# block above, alongside every other --filter test, for the same "Npcap RUNTIME on Windows CI"
# reason; everything else here is offline-read-only and needs no such guard.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -T fields -e <field> (repeatable): prints exactly the requested fields, tab-separated, one
# line per packet, in the order given -- not the field's own position in --format json's output.
# sample_modbus.pcap's own dst_port varies packet to packet (#1 is the HMI's request to the
# PLC's port 502; #2/#3 are the PLC's responses back to the HMI's own ephemeral port 51000) --
# proves real per-packet values are being pulled, not a fixed/cached one.
add_test(NAME fields_basic_selection_tab_separated
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format fields -e index -e protocol -e dst_port --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(fields_basic_selection_tab_separated PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^1\tmodbus\t502\n2\tmodbus\t51000\n3\tmodbus\t51000\n$")

# -T (short form of --format) accepts "fields" as a value too, exactly like --format does --
# same output as the long-form test above, just spelled the tshark way.
add_test(NAME fields_dash_T_short_form_accepts_fields_value
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -T fields -e protocol -e dst_port --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(fields_dash_T_short_form_accepts_fields_value PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^modbus\t502\nmodbus\t51000\nmodbus\t51000\n$")

# A field name this packet's own JSON never populates (either because it doesn't exist at all,
# or -- like src_ip on a raw ARP frame, which has no IP layer -- it's a real JSON key but a
# `null` value for this particular protocol) prints as an empty column, not an error and not the
# literal text "null" -- mirrors tshark's own -e behavior for an absent field.
add_test(NAME fields_missing_field_prints_empty_column
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format fields -e protocol -e totally_bogus_field_xyz -e src_ip --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(fields_missing_field_prints_empty_column PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^arp\t\t\n"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "null")

# --format fields with no -e/--field at all has nothing to print -- caught at CLI-parse-adjacent
# validation time (run_decode, before the packet source even opens), same "fail fast on bad
# setup" posture as an invalid --time-offset -- not a silent empty run.
add_test(NAME fields_format_without_any_field_is_an_error
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --format fields --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(fields_format_without_any_field_is_an_error PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error: --format fields \\(-T fields\\) needs at least one -e/--field")

# -e/--field given without --format fields is very likely a mistake (the field selection has
# nowhere to go under text/json/csv), so it's flagged with an explanatory note rather than
# silently ignored -- but the run itself still proceeds normally (exit 0, ordinary text output),
# since -e isn't inherently invalid outside -T fields, just a no-op there.
add_test(NAME fields_dash_e_without_fields_format_notes_and_continues
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -e protocol --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_modbus.pcap")
set_tests_properties(fields_dash_e_without_fields_format_notes_and_continues PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "note: -e/--field only applies with --format fields \\(-T fields\\); ignoring.*\\[modbus\\]")

# -c is `decode`'s own short alias for --max-packets (mirrors tshark's own -c): stops after
# exactly 2 of sample_arp.pcap's 6 packets.
add_test(NAME dash_c_alias_for_max_packets_stops_early
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -c 2 --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(dash_c_alias_for_max_packets_stops_early PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 .*\n#2 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3 ")

# -a is `decode`'s own short alias for --duration (mirrors tshark's own -a autostop, specialized
# to duration only here) -- --duration only ever bounds a LIVE capture (-i), so on an offline
# read (-r) it's simply accepted and has no effect; this just confirms -a parses cleanly as an
# alias rather than erroring or being mistaken for a positional/other flag.
add_test(NAME dash_a_alias_parses_cleanly_on_offline_read
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -a 5 --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(dash_a_alias_parses_cleanly_on_offline_read PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1 .*#6 "
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "error:")

# -x prints a hex+ASCII dump of each packet's raw bytes below its normal decode line -- offset/
# hex/ASCII columns, 16 bytes per line, matching write_hex_ascii_dump's own layout (output.cpp).
# sample_arp.pcap's own packet #1 is a 42-byte ARP request broadcast to ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff --
# the dump's first line must show that destination MAC's raw bytes and the printable "." fallback
# for non-ASCII bytes, and there must be a second (0010) and a short, space-padded third (0020,
# only 10 bytes) line for a 42-byte frame.
add_test(NAME hex_dump_dash_x_shows_offset_hex_and_ascii_columns
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -c 1 -x --format text --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hex_dump_dash_x_shows_offset_hex_and_ascii_columns PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\\[arp\\][^\n]*\n0000  ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 0c  29 11 22 33 08 06 00 01[^\n]*\n0010 [^\n]*\n0020  00 00 00 00 00 00 c0 a8 +01 0a +")

# -x is ignored (no dump printed) under --format json/csv/fields and under --stats -- none of
# those have a per-packet text line to attach a hex dump below, mirroring tshark's own -x being a
# text/pdml-style reading aid rather than a structured field.
add_test(NAME hex_dump_dash_x_ignored_under_json_format
  COMMAND conduitscope decode -c 1 -x --format json --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap")
set_tests_properties(hex_dump_dash_x_ignored_under_json_format PROPERTIES
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^0000  ")

# -w writes every packet reaching this run to a new classic-pcap file, raw and unmodified --
# proven end to end by round-tripping: write sample_arp.pcap's own 6 packets out through -w, then
# read the written file straight back in and diff its --format json output against the
# original's own --format json output. Byte-identical JSON (same src_mac/dst_mac/summary/etc.
# for all 6 packets, in the same order) is only possible if -w genuinely wrote real, complete,
# correctly-ordered packet records rather than truncating, reordering, or corrupting anything --
# see pcap_writer.cpp's own file header for the classic-pcap format itself. Uses `diff` (not a
# PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, which can't compare two command outputs against each other) via the
# same `bash -c` two-command pattern inventory_iec104_policy_out_round_trips_compliant already
# established elsewhere in this file for an analogous write-then-reread proof.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_round_trips_byte_identical_json
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' --write '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_roundtrip.pcap' --output /dev/null && diff <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' --format json) <('$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_roundtrip.pcap' --format json)")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_round_trips_byte_identical_json PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "^$")

# `info` (its own dedicated summary command, distinct from `decode --stats`) reads the written
# file's own pcap global header back -- confirms -w wrote a genuinely well-formed 24-byte classic
# pcap header (correct magic/version, and the right link type/packet count), not just something
# `conduitscope decode` alone happens to tolerate.
add_test(NAME pcap_write_dash_w_produces_valid_pcap_header
  COMMAND bash -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' decode --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_arp.pcap' -w '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_header_check.pcap' --output /dev/null && '$<TARGET_FILE:conduitscope>' info --read '${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/dash_w_header_check.pcap'")
set_tests_properties(pcap_write_dash_w_produces_valid_pcap_header PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "pcap version: +2\\.4\nlink type: +Ethernet\nsnaplen: .*\npackets: +6")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IPv6 support (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md ROADMAP item 24) -- ipv6.hpp/ipv6.cpp's own base-header and
# RFC 8200 extension-header-chain parsing, format_ipv6's RFC 5952 canonical rendering, and
# decoder.cpp's shared version-sniffing dispatch (Decoder::decode_ip_payload, reached from either
# the IPv4 or the IPv6 branch), all exercised through real Modbus/TCP and plain UDP traffic --
# tests/sample_ipv6.pcap (tools/make_sample_pcap.py's build_ipv6_sample). Every regex below was
# confirmed against the real CLI output first, not guessed at.

# Packet 1: Modbus/TCP request over IPv6, no extension headers -- proves the whole upper-layer
# cascade (TCP dispatch, port-based Modbus recognition) is reachable over IPv6 at all, and that
# both addresses (each with one compressible zero run) render in RFC 5952 canonical form.
add_test(NAME ipv6_modbus_over_tcp_decodes_with_canonical_zero_run_compression
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_modbus_over_tcp_decodes_with_canonical_zero_run_compression PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  2001:db8::50:51000 -> 2001:db8::10:502")

# Packet 2: the response, paired to packet 1 via tcp_session_key/DecodeContext::session_key --
# proves the '#' flow-key/session-key separator fix (decoder.cpp's format_flow_endpoint, added
# alongside this same IPv6 work to remove a latent collision now that an IP address string can
# itself contain colons) didn't break authoritative TCP-session+transaction-ID pairing, the one
# existing feature that most directly depends on session_key uniqueness.
add_test(NAME ipv6_modbus_tcp_session_pairing_works_across_ipv6_addresses
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_modbus_tcp_session_pairing_works_across_ipv6_addresses PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "authoritative pairing: response to transaction id 1")

# Packet 3: a plain UDP datagram over IPv6 between two link-local addresses -- proves has_udp/
# src_port/dst_port populate correctly off an IPv6 outer header.
add_test(NAME ipv6_udp_datagram_decodes_with_link_local_addresses
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_udp_datagram_decodes_with_link_local_addresses PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  2\\.002000  fe80::1:34567 -> fe80::2:44444")

# Packet 4: the same Modbus request as packet 1, preceded by a chained Hop-by-Hop Options header
# and a Destination Options header -- proves parse_ipv6's extension-header walk correctly reaches
# the real upper-layer protocol AND the real payload past two extension headers (the request's own
# "read 4 holding register" text, unique to this packet, only decodes correctly if the walk landed
# exactly on the start of the TCP segment, not a few bytes short or long). Also exercises
# NO_COMPRESSION_ADDR (no zero run at all) to prove format_ipv6 renders plain colon-separated
# groups, with no "::", when there's nothing to compress.
add_test(NAME ipv6_extension_header_chain_walked_to_reach_modbus_payload
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_extension_header_chain_walked_to_reach_modbus_payload PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4  3\\.003000  2001:db8:1:2:3:4:5:6:51001 -> 2001:db8::10:502.*read 4 holding register")

# Packet 5: next_header == ESP directly off the base header, no extension headers at all -- proves
# parse_ipv6 deliberately does NOT walk past ESP (its payload is encrypted, the same opaque-
# regardless-of-IP-version limit ESP already has over IPv4): it must surface as a recognized-but-
# undecoded ESP packet via decoder.cpp's existing GRE/ESP/AH/IPIP/6in4/L2TPv3 tunnel_vpn
# recognition, now reachable over IPv6 with no new code of its own.
add_test(NAME ipv6_esp_next_header_not_walked_past_reaches_tunnel_vpn_recognition
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6.pcap" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_esp_next_header_not_walked_past_reaches_tunnel_vpn_recognition PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#5  4\\.004000  2001:db8::50 -> 2001:db8::10.*SPI=0x12345678")

# A raw-IP link type (no Ethernet framing, no ethertype field at all) carrying an IPv6 packet --
# proves decoder.cpp's version-sniff (peeking the IP version nibble directly) works with no
# ethertype hint to lean on at all, the scenario ROADMAP item 24 specifically calls out.
# tests/sample_ipv6_raw_link.pcapng (build_ipv6_raw_link_sample).
add_test(NAME ipv6_over_raw_ip_link_type_decodes_via_version_sniff
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ipv6_raw_link.pcapng" --format text)
set_tests_properties(ipv6_over_raw_ip_link_type_decodes_via_version_sniff PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  0\\.000000  2001:db8::50:51000 -> 2001:db8::10:502")

# InformationReport -- a DSTransferSet's own periodic/exception report carrying the

# GE SRTP (Service Request Transport Protocol), GE Fanuc/GE Intelligent Platforms PLC families
# (90-30/90-70/RX3i/RX7i) -- see ge_srtp.hpp's own extensive header comment for the four-source
# sourcing, the full wire format, and (notably) the writeup of two real protocol-collision bugs
# against the existing TPKT/COTP decoder found and fixed while building this decoder.
# tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap (build_ge_srtp_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py). Packet #2 (INIT_ACK)
# reuses real captured bytes from automayt/ICS-pcap's GE-SRTP/Notes.txt; every other packet is
# synthetic (no real public GE SRTP pcap capture is known to exist).

# EXTENDED_ACK response -- THE COLLISION-FIX REGRESSION TEST. Before the fix, GE SRTP's own
# declared-length function returned nullopt for EXTENDED_ACK (its body layout past the common
# header is not independently verified by any source, so no length was claimed), which let
# TPKT/COTP's weaker structural gate opportunistically claim this packet instead (GE SRTP's own
# Packet Type 3 supplies TPKT's magic version byte 0x03 by coincidence) and corrupt every
# subsequent server->client packet on the flow into a bogus ongoing TPKT reassembly. This packet
# must show [ge-srtp] with its honestly-undecoded body, NOT [tcp] buffering a TPKT/COTP PDU.
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_extended_ack_undecoded_body_and_tpkt_collision_fix
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_extended_ack_undecoded_body_and_tpkt_collision_fix PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#18  [^\n]*\\[ge-srtp\\]  EXTENDED_ACK response \\(14 byte\\(s\\) from byte 42 onward, layout not independently verified -- see ge_srtp\\.hpp\\)[^\n]*\n *note: matched to the write task memory request seen in packet #17"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#18[^\n]*TPKT")

# UNKNOWN (Packet Type 8) -- structural recognition of a packet type this decoder cannot further
# classify, honestly undecoded rather than guessed at.
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_unknown_packet_type_structural_recognition
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a payload whose Packet Type (256) is not one of GE SRTP's own recognized
# values {0,1,2,3,8} must be REJECTED by GE SRTP's own gate and must NOT be misclassified as any
# other opportunistic protocol either (this exact payload's leading byte, chosen deliberately,

add_test(NAME ge_srtp_gate_rejects_invalid_packet_type_and_falls_through_cleanly
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#21[^\n]*\\[(ge-srtp|mqtt)\\]")

# THE OTHER COLLISION-FIX REGRESSION TEST: a SHORT request's response split across two TCP
# segments, first segment only 20 of 56 bytes. Before the two-phase declared-length fix, GE
# SRTP's own function required the full 56 bytes before it could read Message Type (byte 31) and
# determine shape, so on this short first segment it returned nullopt unconditionally --
# letting TPKT/COTP's weaker gate win the race and misclassify the buffering state. Must show
# "buffering a GE SRTP message PDU/frame", not "buffering a TPKT/COTP PDU/frame".
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_short_first_segment_reassembly_two_phase_declaration_fix
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_short_first_segment_reassembly_two_phase_declaration_fix PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#23  [^\n]*buffering a GE SRTP message PDU/frame split across TCP segments 18245->53600: 20 of 56 declared byte\\(s\\) seen so far across 1 segment\\(s\\) on this flow, waiting for more"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#23[^\n]*TPKT")
add_test(NAME ge_srtp_reassembled_from_two_tcp_segments
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_ge_srtp.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(ge_srtp_reassembled_from_two_tcp_segments PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#24  [^\n]*\\[ge-srtp\\]  SHORT_ACK response: No error[^\n]*\n *note: reassembled a GE SRTP message PDU/frame from 56 byte\\(s\\) spanning 2 TCP segments on this flow\n *note: matched to the read system memory request seen in packet #22")

# Non-standard port (9999, not 18245) in Auto (port-gated) mode: GE SRTP's own GateKind::TcpPort

# BSAP (Bristol Standard Asynchronous/Synchronous Protocol, Bristol Babcock/Emerson RTU protocol)
# recognition -- see bsap.hpp's own file header comment for the full sourcing writeup (including
# why this decoder treats the "BSAAP" name Jurgen pointed at as a naming variant of BSAP), the
# honestly-stated sourcing gap (no numeric RDB function-code table found anywhere, not even in the
# reference open-source Zeek parser this project cross-checked the header layout against), and the
# real dispatch-ordering collision (against both HART-IP's and FF-HSE's own fully opportunistic
# UDP checks) found and fixed via this project's own mandatory manual-CLI-verification-before-
# writing-any-CTest-regex discipline. tests/sample_bsap.pcap (build_bsap_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) is entirely synthetic -- the pcap Jurgen pointed at
# (github.com/EmreEkin/ICS-Pcaps/tree/master/BSAAP) could not be browsed by this session's web
# tools (GitHub's robots.txt blocks directory listings).

# CC-Link IE Field Network Basic (CCIEFB) -- see cclink_ie.hpp's own file header for the full
# sourcing/scoping/design writeup. These tests exercise both message families (cyclic data on UDP
# 61450, SLMP node search/set-IP-address on UDP 61451) plus the critical MELSEC-coexistence design:
# a genuine MELSEC command riding the same 3E framing must not be swallowed (packet #8 below), and
# an orphan CC-Link IE response with no session-tracked request must fall through to MELSEC's own
# generic response handling rather than being misattributed (packet #7 below).
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_cyclic_request_recognized

# Orphan response, no session-tracked request (fresh 4-tuple) -- MUST fall through to MELSEC's own
# generic response handling, not be claimed/misattributed as cclink-ie. This is the direct proof of
# cclink_ie.hpp's own "RESPONSES CARRY NO COMMAND FIELD" design.
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_orphan_response_falls_through_to_melsec
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_orphan_response_falls_through_to_melsec PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#7  [^\n]*\\[melsec\\]  MELSEC response: Normal completion[^\n]*\n *note: no outstanding request found on this session"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#7  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

# A genuine MELSEC command (Batch Read, command 0x0401) riding the exact same 3E framing and port
# this decoder is tried on -- the direct zero-regression proof: 0x0401 is not one of this decoder's
# own 3 known commands, so it must still decode [melsec], never [cclink-ie].
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_genuine_melsec_command_not_swallowed
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_genuine_melsec_command_not_swallowed PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[melsec\\]  Batch Read request: D100, 1 point\\(s\\), word units"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

# Same genuine MELSEC command, but with --protocol cclink-ie forced -- the sharpest proof of all:
# this decoder's own gate rejects it outright (command 0x0401 doesn't match 0x0E70/0x0E30/0x0E31),
# so forcing cclink-ie still correctly falls through to generic [udp], never fabricating a match.
add_test(NAME cclink_ie_forced_protocol_still_rejects_genuine_melsec_command
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --protocol cclink-ie --format text)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_forced_protocol_still_rejects_genuine_melsec_command PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[udp\\]  UDP payload of 21 byte\\(s\\)"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#8  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]")

add_test(NAME cclink_ie_cyclic_response_non_success_end_code
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_cclink_ie.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_cyclic_response_non_success_end_code PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#10  [^\n]*\\[cclink-ie\\]  CC-Link IE Field Basic cyclic response: slave=192.168.1.10 group=1 seq=2 end_code=CCIEFB: error in slave station[^\n]*\n *note: CCIEFB cyclic response reports a non-success end code[^\n]*\n *note: matched to the request seen in packet #9")

add_test(NAME cclink_ie_non_standard_port_note

set_tests_properties(cclink_ie_non_standard_port_note PROPERTIES

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a 2-byte payload carrying only the 3E-frame request magic -- too short for

# attack_detect.hpp -- classic network-layer DoS/reconnaissance attack signatures (see its own
# file header for the full sourcing/scoping writeup). sample_attack_detect.pcap (build_attack_detect_sample,
# tools/make_sample_pcap.py) carries one positive + (where the false-positive risk is real) one
# negative-control packet per single-packet/fragment-pair structural signature, plus 6-packet runs
# per flood category exercised with --flood-threshold 5 (the real default, 100, is deliberately
# NOT sized into this fixture -- see attack_detect.hpp's own DEFAULT_FLOOD_THRESHOLD comment for
# why 100 was chosen empirically against this codebase's own largest existing single-destination
# fixture, sample_samr_lsarpc.pcap's 79 packets).

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: a flood targeting a broadcast-looking destination is never flagged, even at
# the same low --flood-threshold 5 the positive flood tests above use -- see
# attack_detect.hpp's flood_counters_for comment (a flood targets one specific host by
# definition; broadcast reuse is the same shape sample_bacnet.pcap's own routine broadcast
# traffic has, and colliding with it was a real regression this feature's own manual-
# verification pass caught and fixed -- see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#(48|49|50|51|52|53)  [^\n]*\n *note:.*flood suspected")

# NEGATIVE CONTROL: the REAL default threshold (100, no --flood-threshold override) never fires
# against this fixture's own 6-packet-per-category flood runs -- proves --flood-threshold 5 above
# is actually doing something, not just testing an already-guaranteed-to-fire condition.

# codesys.hpp/.cpp -- CODESYS V3 (3S-Smart/CODESYS GmbH's PLC runtime protocol), added at Jurgen's
# request. See codesys.hpp's own file header for the full sourcing (a public Wireshark dissector
# plus Kaspersky ICS-CERT's own reverse-engineering research), scoping (decided via
# AskUserQuestion: V3 only, structural-only beyond CmpDevice's own Login/AUTH exchange), and wire
# format writeup. sample_codesys.pcap (build_codesys_sample, tools/make_sample_pcap.py) carries 8
# TCP messages (OPEN_CHANNEL req/resp, Login/AUTH req/resp, a structural-only CmpApp command, a
# non-validating BLK continuation-block fallback, a non-standard-port variant, and a negative
# control) plus 4 UDP datagrams (Address Service, Channel Service GET_INFO on a standard and a
# non-standard port, and a negative control).
add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_open_channel_request_and_response
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_open_channel_request_and_response PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#1  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service; channel OPEN_CHANNEL ch=1[^\n]*\n#2  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service; channel OPEN_CHANNEL response ch=1")

# Login/AUTH request: username decoded, password field NEVER rendered (presence/length only),
# regardless of Kaspersky's own "encrypted" characterization -- mirrors this codebase's own
# NL_TRUST_PASSWORD/SAMR-style never-render-credential-bytes convention. FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION
# checks the raw password bytes never leak into the text output in any form.
add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_login_auth_username_decoded_password_never_rendered
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_login_auth_username_decoded_password_never_rendered PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#3  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service; channel BLK ch=1; CmpDevice::Login \\(AUTH\\) session=0 user=\"engineer\"[^\n]*\n *note: Login/AUTH request carries a password field \\(10 byte\\(s\\)\\) -- never rendered by this decoder regardless of whether it is genuinely encrypted on the wire"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s3cr3t")

add_test(NAME codesys_tcp_login_auth_response_session_id
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format text -v)
set_tests_properties(codesys_tcp_login_auth_response_session_id PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "#4  [^\n]*\\[codesys\\]  CODESYS TCP Channel Service; channel BLK ch=1; CmpDevice::Login \\(AUTH\\) session=0 new_session=1245391901")

add_test(NAME codesys_json_fields_auth_request
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(codesys_json_fields_auth_request PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"codesys_component\": \"CmpDevice\",\n *\"codesys_command\": \"Login \\(AUTH\\)\",\n *\"codesys_session_id\": 0,\n *\"codesys_encrypted\": false,\n *\"codesys_auth_username\": \"engineer\",\n *\"codesys_auth_password_present\": true,"
  FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "s3cr3t|codesys_auth_password\"|codesys_auth_password_length")

add_test(NAME codesys_json_fields_auth_response
  COMMAND conduitscope decode --read "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/sample_codesys.pcap" --format json)
set_tests_properties(codesys_json_fields_auth_response PROPERTIES
  PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "\"codesys_component\": \"CmpDevice\",\n *\"codesys_command\": \"Login \\(AUTH\\)\",\n *\"codesys_session_id\": 0,\n *\"codesys_encrypted\": false,\n *\"codesys_auth_session_id\": 1245391901,")

# CmpApp with an unrecognized command ID -- structural-only per the AskUserQuestion scoping
# decision: component named, command shown as a raw number, payload never tag-walked.
